Sports.title: Kim's 59 falls one shot short of equalling PGA Tour record
Sports.content:
Michael Kim sensationally recorded only the 16th sub-60 score in the history of the PGA Tour as he shot a 12-under par 59 to shoot up the leaderboard at the 3M Open on Friday.

Kim's flawless round included a string of consecutive birdies between holes three and seven, before he wrapped up his round in style, going four under for his final four holes.

The American's putter was red hot on Friday, draining eight putts from 10 or more feet away from the hole, and wrapped up his round in style, with an incredible 24-foot putt for birdie on the 18th.

Image: Kim, holding up his scorecard, hit 12 birdies and no bogeys on his way to a flawless 12-under par 59 during his second round

The previous low round on the PGA Tour for the 2026 season was 60, with five players, Blades Brown, Wyndham Clark, Si Woo Kim, Andrew Putnam and Scottie Scheffler, all having achieved the feat this season.

Kim's second-round 59 puts him joint-second for the lowest 18-hole scores in PGA Tour history, with Jim Furyk's fourth-round 58 at the 2016 Travelers Championship remaining the US circuit's record score.

The 33-year-old, whose lone victory on the PGA Tour came at the 2018 John Deere Classic, explained he felt like he left everything out on the golf course.

"I putted awesome," he said. "I feel that I got just about everything I could out of that round.

"Some shots I didn't feel supremely confident over, but that's golf. I was happy I got away with par on 13.

"But other parts of my game, like my putting, felt fantastic. When you hit a putt and it does exactly what you kind of envisioned before you hit it, it's an awesome feeling. Felt like that all day out there."

Sports.title: Maresca says managing Manchester City ‘a privilege’ but admits challenge of following Guardiola
Sports.content:
Enzo Maresca said following Pep Guardiola as Manchester City manager is a “privilege” but admitted he is aware how the successors to Sir Alex Ferguson and Arsène Wenger struggled at Manchester United and Arsenal.

Maresca took over at City last month and, at his first press conference in the role, said he understands the challenge of replacing Guardiola, who claimed 17 major trophies in his decade in charge to become the club’s greatest ever manager.

The Italian said: “First of all, I have to say that it’s a privilege because the club decided to go for me. I said many times that I consider Pep probably the best coach in the world in the last 20, 25 years.”

Maresca pointed to how United dipped when David Moyes replaced Ferguson, who was in charge for 26 and a half years, in May 2013. Arsenal also struggled when Wenger departed after 22 years in May 2018, being replaced by Unai Emery.

Maresca said: “It’s a challenge. It’s nice. Also, the history of the manager with many years in the same club always struggled a little bit. After Sir Alex, after Arsène. But also, it’s a challenge to try to do the right things immediately for this organisation, for the fans, for everyone.”

Maresca believes City’s structure gives him the best chance of success. “The organisation is the main thing. This club, this organisation, they had three managers in 17 years,” he said of Guardiola, Manuel Pellegrini and Roberto Mancini. “This is not normal. It doesn’t happen often.

“I’m confident that we can do a great job. We can continue to do the job that has been done since Roberto was here, then after Manuel and for 10 years Pep.”

Maresca confirmed that Rodri will have back surgery on Monday, so is set to miss the start of the season. The new City manager was asked whether the 30-year-old’s future remains at the club, with Real Madrid considering a move for the player.

“First of all, around big players there is always speculation,” Maresca said. “I’m not worried about that. Also because they [Spain] won the World Cup and he was the best player or one of the best players, I think every manager wants to have Rodri because he’s a top player.

“But now he has surgery on, I think, Monday. He needs holiday, rest. Then he will be back here with us.”

The manager added that James Trafford, the second-choice goalkeeper who is of interest to Leeds, and Jack Grealish, who has returned to City after last season’s loan at Everton, could both depart.

Maresca said: “Jack, at the moment, he’s a Man City player. I always said the same – in any club I join, I like to know if there are players that belong to the club, it’s my duty to try to coach them. Then we see what happens.

“I know James because he was my keeper when I was with the City Under-23s [in 2020-21]. But again, when the transfer window is open now, January, anything can happen. So we see. But at the moment, he’s one of our keepers.”

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp vows to change Germany but threatens to quit if family hounded by media
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp said he wants his team to “change a country” after being confirmed as Germany’s new head coach, but threatened to stand down if his family are hounded by the media during his time in charge.

In a forthright first press conference upon his unveiling as Julian Nagelsmann’s replacement, Klopp also suggested the role will be his final job in top-level football and expressed regret after poking fun at his predecessor while working as a television pundit during the World Cup. He is tasked with reviving Germany, who lost to Paraguay in the last 32 and have not made the last 16 since winning the tournament in 2014.

It marks a return to the dugout for Klopp two years after leaving Liverpool, where he ended a glorious nine-season tenure after explaining he felt fatigued. Since January 2025 he has worked as head of global soccer for Red Bull but a comeback to frontline action had appeared inevitable since Nagelsmann departed on 3 July.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp was in forthright mood in his first press conference as Germany head coach. Photograph: Hannes Albert/EPA

Klopp vowed to transform a deeply fractured relationship between the national team and Germany’s public, citing his work at Liverpool as an example of the way football can galvanise a wider community.

“I want to create a situation where fans go home after the game and say: ‘Wow, that was cool,’” he said. “I want people to say: ‘Wow, it was worth putting the TV on for 90 minutes to see Germany play.’ I’ve lived and experienced how football can change a city. And I think it’s not only about cities, it’s also about the country. Ideally, football can change a country.”

The 59-year-old’s contract will run until after the 2030 World Cup. Klopp, however, warned that he would not tolerate invasive treatment from journalists and that he would be prepared to depart without compensation if he felt his family’s privacy had been violated.

“I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you treated Nagelsmann,” he said. “I’m taking this job even though I’ve seen how you’ve treated, in England, Thomas Tuchel. The day you don’t want me any more, I’m gone, without any severance pay. If you say tomorrow: ‘He’s shit,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away.

“Criticise me if something doesn’t work. Jürgen Klopp is not going to have any career after the national team. This is the pinnacle of my career as a coach. I will give it everything I’ve got.”

Klopp was criticised last month when, speaking with the former Germany player Thomas Müller on television during coverage of the group stage match with Curaçao, he appeared to hint Nagelsmann’s days were numbered by saying he was “still” picking the team. That was followed by a quick apology; Klopp repeated the sentiment on Friday and said the pair have yet to speak since his appointment was confirmed.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp, in his role as Magenta TV pundit, with Kylian Mbappé after France’s World Cup quarter-final against Morocco. Photograph: Greg M Cooper/EPA

“We haven’t had any exchange,” he said, wishing Nagelsmann a happy 39th birthday for Thursday. “It was a joke. In retrospect it was one of the worst ‘funny’ remarks I have ever made. I feel awfully sorry, I’ve apologised a million times.

“It was just a rash thing to say, with no ulterior motive whatsoever, and I can only wish him the best.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Now he can go on to pastures new and I’m absolutely sure he will have many opportunities to coach a big team in future.”

Klopp promised Germany will play expansive football with wingers but admitted they must find their own way to compete with the depth of talent available elsewhere. “Success is performance relative to expectations,” he said. “When we ask in Germany: ‘Are we as good as France?’ and the answer is no, that’s not true. If we ask: ‘Do we have players like Dembélé, Mbappé, Doué and Barcola?’, no we don’t, but we can still beat them.

“We don’t want to play like Argentina, Spain, England or France. We want to do it the German way, very intense. Are we the No 1 team right now? No, we accept that. There are 11 teams ahead of us in the ranking. We can beat them, but for this to happen we need to play very good, very intense football.”

International football will demand a change of rhythm for Klopp after a lifetime spent in the domestic game. “I think contact with a team is not necessarily about working with them day in, day out,” he said. “Sometimes it will be 30 minutes or an hour and that will be on the pitch. But all of them have a mobile. I’ll talk to them, listen to them, watch games and give my feedback. That, too, is developing players and making them better.”

Klopp’s reign will begin with a ­baptism of fire in Amsterdam against the Netherlands on 24 September, one of four Nations League games in the space of 11 days. “The players have to show me, and not just say it, that playing for Germany is a super special thing,” he said.

Sports.title: Football Daily | Manchester United and the quest to make mythical midfield a reality
Sports.content:
MIDDLE MEN

Like the urban myth that you are never more than three feet away from a spider, modern footballing lore tells us Manchester United are only ever three signings away from a Premier League title challenge. With the Geopolitics World Cup in the rear-view mirror and the transfer news machine churning once more, you may have missed United being linked with just about every midfielder to ever grace a centre circle. They missed out on Elliot Anderson – who went and dubbed his new club the “kings of Manchester” – and were fooled into thinking they could snare Aurélien Tchouaméni. They danced briefly with Atalanta’s Éderson, before landing on Chelsea resale project prospect Andrey Santos and former Aston Villa linchpin Youri Tielemans. And United aren’t done with their midfield overhaul – rightly so given they have lost Casemiro to Inter Miami and Manuel Ugarte to long-term knee knack. Next up on United’s extensive longlist: Real Madrid’s Eduardo Camavinga and Fulham’s Sander Berge, plus France GWC sensation Manu Koné as Michael Carrick eyes the final piece in his midfield puzzle.

The problem with United over the past 13 years has been that it’s never actually the final piece. It would be kind to call their post-Ferguson transfer hit rate scattergun. Ángel Di María was the first final piece in the puzzle. Then it was Alexis Sánchez. Then Fred. And then Jadon Sancho. Something needed to change. So say what you like about Big Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s recent, purse-tightening Old Trafford regime, but they’ve not flopped anywhere near as hard in the transfer market as their predecessors. Only Ugarte and Joshua Zirkzee can be deemed true flops under the Ineos boys. Bryan Mbeumo and Matheus Cunha were smart additions a year ago, Senne Lammens was a scouting triumph and United are threatening to go again with their sensible signings policy – who’d have thunk it?! – with a combined £85m on Santos and Tielemans representing far better value than splashing that same amount on relegation specialist Matheus Fernandes. Finding value in the market is almost impossible nowadays, but credit to these fellas, they’re giving it a go.

What feels quite apt with Carrick at the wheel is that United’s biggest struggle this summer has been to find a true midfield destroyer. That moniker certainly doesn’t fit Santos, nor Tielemans. Tchouaméni was always unattainable so United are getting creative, as they did when Carrick was sought as Roy Keane’s replacement in 2006, less a like-for-like replacement and more a style shift. OK, it could be argued that Berge – an experienced screening No 6 – could step into the Casemiro void after a promising GWC campaign, but Camavinga and Koné like to charge around putting out fires, so perhaps United are following the mould of other top clubs and dispensing with the idea of the Makélélé role.

Modern football is all about excess, whether that be GWC participants, number of games, or transfer fees going beyond £100m for apparently workmanlike players. United have long threatened to descend into financial overspill, but after a steady season under a steady manager, are they finally grasping the concept of modest frugality? Roll up, roll up: ditch the merch-baiting marquee signing and grab yourself three all-purpose midfielders, all for reasonable prices! It surely cannot last.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“This is ideally the high point of my career, of my life, my professional life. I will give it everything I have [but] if you [reporters] tomorrow start saying: ‘He’s sh!t,’ tell me to my face and I’m out. If you behave badly and don’t leave my family in peace, I’m gone, I’ll just turn away” – Jürgen Klopp takes the Germany job and proves that he should still be good for a quote or two.

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp: still got it. Photograph: Markus Ulmer/GES Sportfoto/Getty Images

Sports.title: Newcastle sign Aladji Bamba in £34m deal from Monaco to boost midfield options
Sports.content:
Newcastle have made Aladji Bamba their fourth signing of the summer after the 20-year-old midfielder completed a move from Monaco for a fee that could rise to £34m.

“I’m very happy to be here,” said Bamba. “I was very excited when I heard Newcastle were interested in signing me. I know about the history of the club and I’ve visited the stadium, which is amazing. I can’t wait to be on the pitch.”

Bamba, who has agreed a five-year contract, is Newcastle’s fourth signing this summer aged 20 or under. The France youth midfielder – who made 25 appearances for Monaco last season, impressing in Ligue 1 and the Champions League – joins the former Reims goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen (20), the former Hoffenheim winger Bazoumana Touré (also 20) and the former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur (18). As a natural No 6, Bamba will be expected to compete with Lewis Miley for the midfield anchor role vacated when Sandro Tonali joined Tottenham for an initial £92.5m.

Newcastle’s transfer policy is to sign players aged 24 or under costing, broadly, between £20m and £40m and possessing high resale potential. The idea is to help ensure a club that has recently negotiated a three-year settlement agreement with Uefa after breaching European spending rules remain on the right side of football’s squad investment regulations. “Aladji adds a range of qualities to our midfield with huge potential for growth,” said Eddie Howe, Newcastle’s manager. “His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and is something we believe we can build on.”

Meanwhile, Howe hopes Bruno Guimarães will be at Newcastle to ease Bamba’s adaptation to Premier League life. The Brazil midfielder is wanted by Arsenal and appears keen to join Mikel Arteta’s team. However, the price is a stumbling block. Newcastle’s reluctance to sell their captain dictates they have let it be known through intermediaries that they will reject any offer in the region of £70m for a player who turns 29 in November.

Arsenal have still to make a formal offer and whether they are prepared to go beyond £75m remains to be seen. Much may hinge on whether Guimarães returns to Newcastle from a holiday in Brazil, as planned, next week before joining his teammates at a training camp at La Manga in southern Spain.

Sports.title: Andoni Iraola backs backroom staff to help cure Liverpool’s set-piece ills
Sports.content:
Andoni Iraola has outlined the roles his backroom staff will play in trying to improve Liverpool’s set-piece record next season and admitted he was “very lucky” to inherit a talented coaching team at Bournemouth.

Iraola has brought several members of his Bournemouth backroom team with him to Liverpool since succeeding Arne Slot last month. Tommy Elphick, a boyhood Liverpool fan, and Shaun Cooper have joined as first-team coaches while Iraola’s long-time colleague Pablo de la Torre has arrived as assistant coach. Alejandro Rosalen has taken over as first-team goalkeeping coach after five years with Napoli.

Iraola worked alongside De la Torre in his first coaching job at AEK Larnaca, and again at Rayo Vallecano, and said having trusted confidants alongside him would be invaluable for his first season in charge at Anfield. “For me, it was important they came with me,” said Iraola, who will take charge of his first Liverpool game on Saturday in a pre-season friendly against Sunderland in Nashville. “Pablo is a physical coach but has been with me almost all the years I have been coaching. So, for me, he is much more than a physical coach really. He is an assistant and we know each other very well.

“I was very lucky with Tommy and Shaun when I arrived at Bournemouth. Because I was unlucky to have the issue with my assistant coach Iñigo Pérez [who was denied a work permit when attempting to follow Iraola from Rayo Vallecano to Bournemouth]. After, it worked out very well for him because now he is coaching Villarreal. Maybe we play him in the Champions League.

“But when I had Tommy and Shaun there, we did not feel the need to bring in another assistant. They were very prepared, they were very helpful for me in terms of understanding the English culture, the mentality of the players, what they were used to, what they like in training, even the small details that maybe in Spain are different. Also the experience Tommy has at Aston Villa, Bournemouth, Brighton, Huddersfield; they can be in a closer position to the players. They can feel more identified. I am a little bit older. Some of the players maybe didn’t know I was a player.”

One requirement for Iraola and his backroom staff will be to address Liverpool’s problems at set pieces. Only Bournemouth (26), Crystal Palace (25) and Leeds (24) conceded more set-piece goals than Liverpool’s 23 in what proved Slot’s final season as head coach, having won the title in his first. “They are very good coaches,” said Iraola. “We kind of ­understand the game similarly and they have different roles in the coaching staff, they help with set pieces also. That’s the reason I continued with them.

“Tommy does defensive set plays, Shaun does more offensive, more ­creative ones. But also we are working very well here with the set-piece analyst [Lewis Mahoney], who was very good in the second half of last season. He is already with the club, so they are working on some stuff.”

Sports.title: Argentina behaviour after World Cup final was ‘intolerable’, says De la Fuente
Sports.content:
Spain’s head coach, Luis de la Fuente, has hit out at the “intolerable, unacceptable” behaviour of Argentina players in the immediate aftermath of Sunday’s World Cup final.

At the forefront were Nahuel Molina and Leandro Paredes, who attacked Rodri and Eric García respectively at New York New Jersey Stadium as Spain’s players celebrated winning the World Cup for a second time in the country’s history. Paredes also confronted Spain’s Gavi.

“At the time, I didn’t realise it. I was celebrating, hugging teammates,” De La Fuente told Spanish television. “But in any case, it is intolerable, unacceptable, it cannot be allowed. Players of that stature, whom I praised in the days leading up to the match and continue to praise, who are great players with a tremendous coach, surely they must have felt just as bad as we did seeing those reactions.”

De la Fuente also praised the exemplary behaviour of his own players faced with these “acts of aggression” and “provocations” which he believes could have escalated into more serious incidents.

Although the scenes were filmed and widely shared on social media, they have not yet resulted in any sanctions against the Argentina players. Fifa has opened an investigation into the incidents to determine whether there may have been violations of the world football governing body’s disciplinary code.

Sports.title: From Popp to Diani: 10 women’s transfers you may have missed during the men’s World Cup
Sports.content:
There were a host of big women’s football transfers which were hard to miss across June and July, despite the dominance of the men’s World Cup. Among them were Beth Mead’s move from Arsenal to Manchester City, Mary Earps and Georgia Stanway returning to the Women’s Super League with London City Lionesses and Arsenal, Sam Kerr leaving Chelsea to return to Gotham FC and, most prominently, Alexia Putellas’s game-changing switch from Barcelona to London City.

But here are 10 transfers you might have missed while attention was focused on the action in the US, Canada and Mexico.

Alexandra Popp to Borussia Dortmund

The three-time Champions League winner Alex Popp may be reaching the twilight of her playing career but her move to Borussia Dortmund, signing a three-year contract at the tier-three club, after 14 years with Wolfsburg shows she is not quite ready to hang up her boots. The 35-year-old has been prolific for club and country, scoring 112 goals in 219 games for Wolfsburg and 67 goals in 145 games for Germany prior to her international retirement in 2024. A Borussia Dortmund fan whose “heart beats for this club”, Popp couldn’t pass up the opportunity to assist the development of the women’s team, which was launched in 2020.

Kirsty Hanson to Tottenham

The 28-year-old was a top target for Spurs after a phenomenal fourth season at Aston Villa. Last year Hanson said she was working on adding more goals to her game – come the end of last season she was the third-highest top scorer in the WSL, finishing on 12 in 22 games, which was 43% of Villa’s total tally and only one goal behind second-place Alessia Russo. She heads to a focused Tottenham who are giving their manager, Martin Ho, the tools to push closer to, or even break into, the top four.

Ally Sentnor to Angel City

Sentnor, who was the first overall pick in the 2024 NWSL draft, was the subject of a blockbuster $850,000 (£635,000) trade between Kansas City Current and Angel City on 19 June. She then made her debut for her new side on 3 July, starting a 2-0 win against Orlando Pride. The USA women’s national team player has scored seven goals and provided three assists in 23 international games and, at just 22 years old, has a lot of football ahead of her.

View image in fullscreen Ally Sentnor (right) on the ball for Angel City in a 2-0 win against against Chicago Stars last weekend. Photograph: Shaina Benhiyoun/SPP/Shutterstock

Felicia Schröder to Real Madrid

Many clubs were circling but in the end Felicia Schröder completed a big-money move from Häcken to Real Madrid. Multiple Swedish outlets reported the deal for the 19-year-old forward was worth over 15m Swedish kronor (£1.15m). She attracted attention from across the world as she racked up 91 goals in 128 games for Häcken and starred in Uefa’s inaugural women’s Europa Cup competition, finishing as top scorer with eight goals, four of which came in the two-legged final against Hammarby.

Manaka Matsukubo to Chelsea

The versatile 21-year-old, who can play as a forward or attacking midfielder, joined Chelsea from North Carolina Courage for an undisclosed fee but, as one of the most exciting young talents in the women’s game, it’s unlikely she came cheap. The Japan international scored 11 goals, became the youngest NWSL player to score a hat-trick, and was named NWSL midfielder of the year in 2025. She was up to five goals in nine games in the 2026 season before Chelsea swooped earlier this month.

View image in fullscreen Manaka Matsukubo at her Chelsea unveiling. Photograph: Harriet Lander/Chelsea FC/Getty Images

Johanna Rytting Kaneryd to OL Lyonnes

The 29-year-old won three league titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, including a domestic treble in . Rytting Kaneryd is one of several attacking players to leave Chelsea this summer with Sam Kerr, Guro Reiten and Catarina Macario also having departed as they revamp their front line in an effort to reclaim their WSL crown after Manchester City ended their six-year title-winning run.

Noémie Mouchon to Everton

The loss of the forward Kelly Gago, who has signed for West Ham, has been tempered a little by the arrival of the French striker Noémie Mouchon from Leicester. Mouchon did not have the easiest time at Leicester after arriving from Reims with expectations high. The 23-year-old sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury one month into her first season in the WSL and was ruled out for the remainder of the campaign. She made 16 appearances and scored two goals in the WSL last season but made only two starts. Everton will be hoping she can find the form that helped her to nine goals in 22 games for Reims in the 2023-24 season.

Denise O’Sullivan to Gotham (on loan)

The influential Republic of Ireland midfielder returns to the NWSL with Gotham after six months with Liverpool. The 32-year-old spent 10 seasons in the US before her January move to Liverpool, with Houston Dash and North Carolina Courage (albeit with a number of loan spells in Australia and England). She won the NWSL Shield in 2017 and again in 2018 and 2019 when Courage also secured the NWSL Championship, with O’Sullivan named the side’s MVP in both years. She has 22 goals in 132 games for Ireland.

View image in fullscreen Denise O’Sullivan (right) showing off her close control against Aston Villa last season. Photograph: Nick Taylor/Liverpool FC/Getty Images

Bethany England to Crystal Palace

Bethany England’s Tottenham departure was mourned by fans, with the former Chelsea forward having become the team’s record goalscorer in the WSL with 32 in three-and-a-half seasons, helping them to a first FA Cup final in 2024. The 32-year-old has signed a two-year contract with Crystal Palace, who earned promotion back into the top flight with a second-place finish in WSL2. After four WSL titles, two FA Cups and two League Cups with Chelsea, England brings a wealth of experience to Palace.

Kadidiatou Diani to London City Lionesses

The arrival of Alexia Putellas and Mary Earps has dominated the London City Lionesses transfer talk, while the acquisition of the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes for more than £500,000 has flown somewhat under the radar. The 31-year-old scored 41 goals in 93 games in three seasons for the Champions League giants following her stunning 92 goals in 168 games for Paris Saint-Germain. Michelle Kang, who owns both London City and Lyonnes, will be hoping she brings that edge up front to the ambitious WSL side. They finished sixth last season, their debut campaign in the top flight, nine points behind Tottenham, but they want more and are spending big to make progress.

Sports.title: Socceroos star Cristian Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine during roadside test
Sports.content:
Socceroos forward Cristian Volpato has allegedly tested positive for cocaine after being stopped while driving at almost 50km/h over the speed limit in Sydney.

Volpato was one of Australia’s breakout stars of the 2026 World Cup but is now back in the spotlight after allegedly driving a BMW Coupe at 109km/h in a 60km/h zone across Anzac Bridge about 1.10am on Friday.

The 22-year-old was subjected to a roadside drug test which allegedly returned a positive result for cocaine. A secondary sample of oral fluid was taken for further analysis, while NSW police confirmed it will continue its inquiries.

Volpato was reportedly issued an infringement notice for speeding and has had his international driver’s licence suspended for six months, meaning he cannot drive in New South Wales. He has not been charged with a criminal offence.

Police allege that Volpato was also stopped two hours earlier on Anzac Bridge, west of Sydney’s CBD, and issued an infringement notice after allegedly driving more than 20km/h over the speed limit.

He was subjected to a roadside alcohol breath test at about 11.05pm Thursday, which returned a negative result.

Football Australia has been contacted for comment.

Volpato plays football for Italian club Sassuolo and represented Italy at at under-19 and under-20 level before switching his international allegiance to Australia on the eve of the World Cup.

He made three appearances for the Socceroos at the tournament and provided an attacking threat as the side progressed from the group stage as runners-up before being knocked out by Egypt in the last 32.

Volpato was born and raised in Sydney and played junior football at Sydney United 58, Sydney FC and Western Sydney Wanderers before moving overseas to join Serie A club Roma.

He left Roma after two seasons to join Sassuolo where he has scored seven goals in three seasons, before making his mark with the Socceroos and shaping up as a key to the national side’s future.

Sports.title: Chelsea go back to Villa to poach set-piece coach Austin MacPhee as Maxence Lacroix has medical ahead of £55m move... and Idrissa Gana Gueye leaves Everton for Saudi Arabia: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again - the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Chelsea go back to Villa for set-piece coach MacPhee

Chelsea are raiding Aston Villa once again to sign up set-piece coach Austin MacPhee.

The 46-year-old who has also been working with Portugal's national squad, has been at Villa for five years.

He was first given responsibility for set pieces by Northern Ireland national team coach Michael O'Neill and the team scored 11 goals from set pieces in 10 games to qualify for Euro 2016.

He said his farewells to Villa staff today and will link up with the likes of Morgan Rogers once again at Stamford Bridge after Rogers' £117m move this week.

Austin MacPhee with Portugal captain Cristiano Ronaldo at the World Cup

Moyes pays tribute to Gana Gueye as midfielder leaves Everton for big-money Saudi deal

Idrissa Gana Gueye is poised to take up a lucrative offer to play in Saudi Arabia.

The 36-year-old has now abandoned talks over a new contract with Everton, who confirmed his exit tonight, and as a free agent is in the throes of finalising terms to move to the Saudi Pro League, joining Al-Diriyah.

The Senegal international also had interest from ambitious French side Le Havre but key to his decision apart from the financial gain is a desire to bring up his children in a Muslim country.

Gueye was popular figure at Everton but turns 37 in September.

David Moyes was willing to offer a new contract but wants more energy in his midfield. He has signed Hayden Hackney from Middlesbrough and wants two more for his engine room.

As Everton confirmed Gueye's exit Moyes said: 'His leadership qualities in and around the dressing room proved crucial, particularly in our final season at Goodison. His commitment to the club over many years was exceptional.

'Everyone connected to Everton thanks Gana – he will always be welcome at the club – and we wish him and his family all the very best for the future.'

Idrissa Gana Gueye joined Everton in 2022 and has made 120 league appearances for them

Morita's a Tiger as Hull get their man

Hull City have confirmed the signing of defensive midfielder Hidemasa Morita on a free transfer.

The 31-year-old joins on a two-year deal which includes an option for a third. Morita left Sporting Lisbon as a free agent earlier this summer and had been talks with Leeds United and Ipswich Town.

Garner's a no-go as Everton dig in their heels

Everton insist James Garner is not for sale despite mooted interest from Premier League rivals.

The midfielder signed a new contract last season and was rewarded for his form with a call-up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad.

Aston Villa, Newcastle United and his former club Manchester United have all been linked in recent months but Everton have no desire to sell with the 25-year-old a key part of David Moyes's plans.

A string of Premier League clubs have been linked with James Garner, 25

Como set to increase bid for Chalobah

Como are expected to hold talks with Chelsea tomorrow over an improved offer for defender Trevoh Chalobah.

The England centre back is keen on making the move and the Italians - managed by former Chelsea midfielder Cesc Fabregas - have indicated they would increase their bid closer to Chelsea's valuation of £35million including add ons.

Como have so far proposed £25m.

For more on this story click HERE

Lacroix closes in on £55m Chelsea move

Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today after the Blues agreed a deal for the Crystal Palace defender worth around £55m on Thursday.

As Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week, talks accelerated over a meeting in New York at the weekend.

Chelsea co-owner Behdad Eghbali and Palace chairman Steve Parish, who were in New York for the World Cup final, met at the Aman Hotel near Central Park on Sunday.

Daily Mail Sport revealed Chelsea had revisited their interest in the 26-year-old early this summer.

The France international cost Palace £18m from Wolfsburg but has been an outstanding performer in the Premier League and Europe.

Crystal Palace and France star Maxence Lacroix is undergoing his medical at Chelsea today

Villa in talks to sign Jackson

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea’s Nicolas Jackson.

The clubs have already agreed a loan with obligation deal for Alejandro Garnacho to join Villa. That followed the £117m sale of Morgan Rogers.

The structure of the deals are key as Chelsea and Villa are among those that need to comply with Uefa's squad cost ratio regulations and their 2025 settlement agreements.

Rogers' £117m move will provide Villa with a significant accounting profit, potentially over £80m after Middlesbrough's sell-on clause and the remaining book value of his 2024 signing are deducted.

But if Chelsea had sold Garnacho to Villa as part of the same transaction, Uefa would treat it as a swap deal, impinging on profit margin. Even if Garnacho left on deadline day September 1, that is fewer than the guideline of 45 days, making it harder to argue they are not connected.

A loan with an obligation to buy could still be regarded as part of a swap deal because the 'purchase' has been agreed within 45 days of Rogers' transfer but the conditions give Villa control of when that deal is completed and potential room for manoeuvre with Uefa regulators.

Aston Villa remain in discussions over a move for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson

Summerville's Saudi switch confirmed

Al-Hilal have confirmed the signing of winger Crysencio Summerville from West Ham in a deal worth up to £60million.

The 24-year-old, who also had an offer from Roma, had a medical in Amsterdam on Tuesday.

Al Hilal will pay an initial fee of £55m, plus £5m in potential add-ons.

Magpies get their man

Aladji Bamba will wear the number eight shirt vacated by Sandro Tonali, after completing his £30million move to Newcastle United.

Bamba arrived from Monaco on Thursday and Newcastle will pay a further £5.5m in add-ons.

The 20-year-old has signed a five-year contract and manager Eddie Howe said: 'He's another exciting, young signing who we're really looking forward to working with.

'Aladji adds depth and a range of qualities to our midfield options, with a huge potential for growth.

'His development since breaking through at Monaco has been really impressive and something we believe we can help him build on.

'He operates in a deeper role but has the ability to contribute all over the pitch, which he demonstrated in both Ligue Un and the Champions League last season.'

Meanwhile, Newcastle say they have still to receive a formal offer from Arsenal for Bruno Guimaraes.

No Blues interest in Bruno

Chelsea are not expected to pursue a move for Newcastle United midfielder Bruno Guimaraes.

There had been suggestions that the West London club were interested in the Brazilian international, but Chelsea sources categorically refute this.

Daily Mail Sport understands that Chelsea have not, at any point, enquired about Guimaraes and sources maintain they have no plans to.

BOBBY MANZI

Ex-Burnley star catching Tigers' interest

Hull City are interested in Burnley midfielder Florentino Luis.

The Portuguese was on loan from Benfica last season, but Burnley have just made that move permanent for £20million as their obligation from the original deal.

However, Burnley are also understood to be willing to sell the 26-year-old to recoup funds and salary while they are in the Championship.

Boro target World Cup star

Middlesbrough are in talks to sign USA midfielder Sebastian Berhalter from Vancouver Whitecaps.

Boro are paying £900,000 for the 25-year-old who has 18 caps and played in all of the USA's World Cup games.

The deal includes a further £600,000 in add-ons.

Berhalter was born in London where his father Gregg, a former USA coach, was a player at Crystal Palace.

Boro remain in talks for left-back Max Arfsten from Columbus Crew also.

Sports.title: Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games heat plunged into chaos with star's appearance delayed by 10 minutes - before volunteer strips off to save the day
Sports.content:
Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games heat plunged into chaos with star's appearance delayed by 10 minutes - before volunteer strips off to save the day

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Adam Ramsay-Peaty's Commonwealth Games return was marred by a bizarre delay which held him back from the pool for 10 minutes.

The swimmer, who has added his wife Holly's family surname to his own, made a splash in the 100m breaststroke heats.

Ramsay-Peaty recorded the quickest time of anybody in the heats to qualify for the semi-finals this evening, with the final being tomorrow.

But the 31-year-old, who is targeting a fifth Commonwealth gold medal, had to wait around due to a strange occurrence.

While he was on the blocks, one of the lane dividers broke off, leading to some commotion as the fixing had sunk to the bottom of the pool.

Fortunately, a volunteer was on hand to strip down to his shorts and dive in to amend the problem.

Adam Ramsay-Peaty (not pictured) was delayed on his return to the Commonwealth Games... as a volunteer had to jump in the pool to fix a lane line

The swimmer blasted through his 100m breaststroke heat and is hoping for a fifth Commonwealth gold

Holly Ramsay cheered husband Adam on from the sidelines amid her pregnancy

And none of that put Ramsay-Peaty off his stride as he blasted to a time of 59.46 seconds.

This is his fourth Commonwealth Games – his debut was in 2014 in Glasgow, and he has made the tournament a happy hunting ground with four golds and three silvers.

Alongside the 100m, the three-time Olympic champion will also partake in the 50m breaststroke event.

His wife, Holly, the daughter of celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay, shared a snap to her Instagram Stories of Adam in his new 'Ramsay-Peaty' swimming cap and wrote: 'So Special.'

Holly, a 26-year-old influencer, is pregnant with their child.

Swimmer Ramsay-Peaty's parents did not attend the wedding in December and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them.

Earlier this month, the Daily Mail revealed that Adam's pregnant sister Bethany – the only member of his family to still be in contact with the couple – has now sensationally fallen out with Holly.

The roots of the family conflict go back to September 2024, when Adam and Holly snubbed wider members of the Peaty family by not inviting them to their engagement party.

Holly shared a snap to her Instagram Stories of Adam in the new swimming cap and wrote: 'So Special'

The athlete duly wasted no time in recording the fastest time of the morning, 59.46 seconds

Influencer Holly, 26, announced last month she is expecting a baby girl with Adam

His parents, Caroline and Mark, did not attend the wedding and are assumed to not be attending the Commonwealth Games amid a falling out. Adam remains estranged from them

Join the discussion Could you stay focused after an unexpected delay?

Mother Caroline, who spent years ferrying her son to early-morning training sessions, was also not invited to Holly's glamorous hen do at Soho Farmhouse in the Cotswolds, even though the bride's mother, Tana, and friends including Victoria, were at the extravagant bash.

Adam changing his name to Ramsay-Peaty and registering under the double-barrel surname for the Games in Glasgow is seen by some as the latest blow for his estranged loved ones – especially as Ramsay is placed first before Peaty.

A source said previously: 'Adam may be rich but we have something that he doesn't and that is brains, loyalty, integrity and family.

'Money makes for a cold bedfellow. It can't hold you tight when things go wrong or when you have a bad day.'

They added: 'When you live to be famous you aren't living, you are playing a role. Fame is fleeting but family is forever.'

Adam has described these Games as a 'full circle moment' as he looks to reignite his career.

A silver medal at the Paris Olympics in 2024 helped him refocus after a difficult 2023 in which he withdrew from a series of events in order to focus on mental health concerns.

He credits his Christian faith with saving him and helping him turn his life around.

His win in the 100m in 2014 began eight years of almost total dominance in the event. That streak came to an end in dramatic fashion in Birmingham four years ago when he trailed home in a shock fourth place in the event.

The athlete, who is due to return for his semi-final on Friday evening, told TNT Sports: 'Job done, really. We've got a busy two weeks coming up, so we're reserving energy where we can.

'Last time I was here, I was very young. We barely had any world records to my name, or known world records to my name, so it's been a very long journey.'

Sports.title: LeBron James signs with the Philadelphia 76ers as NBA icon finally makes a decision on his future
Sports.content:
LeBron James has stunned the NBA by signing with the Philadelphia 76ers.

It ends the uncertainty over the NBA icon's future that has dominated the offseason and brings his spell with the Los Angeles Lakers to an end after an eight-season run highlighted by the 2020 NBA title.

James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid, Jaylen Brown and Tyrese Maxey as he pursues an elusive fifth NBA title.

He is set to sign a modest $8 million, two-year contract with the Sixers, according to ESPN. He made nearly $53 million last season.

In a lengthy statement on X, the 41-year-old admitted he strongly considered retiring but believes he still has 'more to give' and can turn his new team into a contender.

He wrote: 'I thought I was done when the season ended. I wasn't ready to announce it, and I knew I needed some time to really decide, but I was pretty sure I played my last game. I was honest at that last press conference when I said I needed to look at myself and deicide if I still love this game.

LeBron James is signing with the Philadelphia 76ers on a two-year, $8 million deal

The 41-year-old, pictured with wife Savannah, has spent the summer deciding his future

James joins a menacing 76ers roster that includes the likes of Joel Embiid and Jaylen Brown

'I still truly love this game, and I have more to give. The last few weeks have really been special. I’ve never been able to have no clue what to do and take real time to just think. I’ve had an incredible few months with all the people I love trying to figure it all out.

'This is my last decision. I’m not going for money. I’m not going for family. What am I really playing for at this point? I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind. I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of winning another championship.

'I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to energize a new fan base and start this incredible journey one last time. Thank you LA. Miami I’ll forever love and Northeast Ohio will always home!'

James told the Lakers earlier this summer that he would not be returning to Los Angeles next season.

Reports claimed that James' former teams, the Cleveland Cavaliers and the Miami Heat, were leading the charge to sign him. He was also heavily linked to the Golden State Warriors.

But James joins a 76ers team that has not won an NBA championship since 1983 and has not advanced out of the second round of the Eastern Conference playoffs since 2001.

Philadelphia fans will be hoping he can wipe out that streak just as he did in Cleveland, who had not won a title for 52 years before he led them to success in 2016.

The Athletic reports that Maxey and other key figures with Philadelphia have been relentlessly pursuing James in recent weeks. Their blockbuster trade for Brown with the Celtics also tipped the balance in their favor.

James, who will turn 42 in December, is about to enter his 24th season in the NBA, which is a league record. He is the all-time leading scorer in NBA history and has won four championships, two with the Heat and once each with the Cavaliers and Lakers.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury stops Mariusz Wach inside seven rounds in Thailand... as Saudi organisers try to rush him to Jeddah for Anthony Joshua's return ahead of proposed British megafight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury stops Mariusz Wach inside seven rounds in Thailand... as Saudi organisers try to rush him to Jeddah for Anthony Joshua's return ahead of proposed British megafight

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Tyson Fury took care of business with the minimum of fuss as he dispatched Mariusz Wach in a low-key contest in Thailand on Friday night - before attention quickly shifted to what is next.

Daily Mail Sport understands the former heavyweight world champion is expected to board a flight to Jeddah after the victory, with Saudi organisers Sela arranging travel in the hope Fury will be in attendance for Anthony Joshua's return against Kristian Prenga on Saturday night.

Fury stopped Wach inside seven rounds of a schedule 10 to emerge victorious on Friday evening, with the Polish fighter retiring on his stool.

The fight - not carried by any major broadcaster - is understood to have been one-sided, with Fury connecting with five uppercuts in a row in the fifth round.

Fury was always expected to come through unscathed against Wach, ranked outside the world's top 200, in what was widely viewed as a stay-busy fight ahead of the biggest assignment of his comeback.

Tyson Fury emerges for the untelevised bout in Pattaya, Thailand

Fury dispatched Wach inside seven rounds in a dominant display

The contest itself attracted little attention compared to a usual Fury fight week but it served its purpose by allowing Fury to continue building momentum before his proposed showdown with Joshua later this year.

The event also raised funds for the Father Ray Foundation, with all the gate receipts from a 1,500 crowd donated to the Pattaya-based charity, which has spent more than 40 years supporting orphans, children with disabilities and underprivileged young people across Thailand.

The focus now turns to whether the Gypsy King will make the trip to Saudi Arabia.

Daily Mail Sport understands Sela have made arrangements for Fury to fly directly from Thailand to Jeddah, where Joshua returns to action on Saturday in his first fight since the devastating car crash that claimed the lives of two friends and members of his close team.

Joshua has described the tragedy as the toughest period of his life and has vowed to continue the work and ambitions of those he lost, while also pledging long-term financial support to their families. His return against Prenga therefore represents far more than simply another outing inside the ring.

Whether Fury and Joshua come face-to-face this weekend, however, remains uncertain.

Fury and Wach were clashing ahead of Fury's proposed megafight with Anthony Joshua

Fury takes the plaudits at the end of the bout, which

... and celebrates in the ring having extended his career record to 36 wins from 39 fights

Fury has insisted in recent interviews that he had no plans to attend the event, despite speculation gathering throughout fight week that he would make the journey after boxing in Thailand.

One possible explanation is what unfolded following Fury's victory over Arslanbek Makhmudov earlier this year.

Joshua, who had been ringside, opted against climbing into the ring afterwards as the contract hadn’t been officially signed, meaning the much-anticipated first face-off between Britain's two biggest heavyweight stars never materialised.

Fury may now be taking a similar approach, choosing not to hand Joshua the moment after his own comeback, despite the paperwork being done.

Even so, there remains hope behind the scenes that the pair will finally share a stage should Joshua come through safely against Prenga.

Sports.title: Falkland Islanders hit out at Lionel Messi and Co over controversial World Cup banner and blast Argentina's 'dirty' and 'deeply unpleasant' antics during tournament
Sports.content:
Falkland Islanders hit out at Lionel Messi and Co over controversial World Cup banner and blast Argentina's 'dirty' and 'deeply unpleasant' antics during tournament

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

On Tuesday morning, a small contingent of Falkland Islanders boarded the South Atlantic Airbridge plane from Mount Pleasant to RAF Brize Norton in Oxfordshire.

The Ministry of Defence commission their only direct flight to the UK so they donned their Commonwealth Games uniform and began the 8,000-mile journey to Glasgow.

‘We didn’t really have an international airstrip when Argentina invaded in 1982,’ explained Mike Summers OBE, the Chairman of the National Sports Council in the Falkland Islands. ‘We could fly through Argentina but there was no proper service.

‘The UK government built an international airstrip after the war. Now civilians have access to an RAF flight, run by a company called AirTanker. It operates twice a week but it’s rarely full, so you get plenty of space!’

Rest assured, the island’s team of six bowlers suffered no leg room issues, well rested to fly their Blue Ensign flag in Scotland.

When they were paraded into the Hydro arena for the opening ceremony, Andy Burnham muttered something into Queen Camilla’s ear that triggered chuckles in the royal enclosure. We may never know what the new Prime Minister said but there is a strong chance it related to Argentina’s football team.

The Falkland Islands have become a focus after Argentina’s players lifted a controversial banner after beating England at the World Cup

Thanks to Lionel Messi and Co, the British Overseas Territory is caught in the middle of a high-profile sovereignty dispute. After their World Cup semi-final victory over England, they celebrated with a banner reading, ‘Las Malvinas son Argentinas’, which translates to ‘The Falklands are Argentine’.

The bowls team have become unlikely spokespeople.

‘Sport and politics shouldn’t mix,’ said Kris Thorsen, after her first-round defeat by Malaysia on Friday morning. It is safe to say that Thorsen and her team-mate, Sharon Barnes, are not too familiar with the diplomatic spotlight.

Summers, however, offered a more forthright opinion.

‘Everybody in the Falklands was watching the World Cup,’ Summers told the Daily Mail Sport. ‘The majority of people would support England, apart from the odd Scot or Welshman. It’s the same with the rugby and the same with the cricket. Here in Glasgow, we would support Adam Peaty if he were swimming against an Australian or a South African.

‘When Messi and his team-mates were holding that banner we thought, “What the hell are they doing? This is a football match”. We’ve seen that banner before, of course. Half of those guys play their football in the Premier League. They are paid very large salaries which are taxed at a high rate to pay for the UK defence!

‘We’re very disappointed with their antics and their dirty play. Their attitude was deeply unpleasant. The World Cup will never be as friendly as the Commonwealth Games but, by and large, teams manage to shake hands afterwards. Six of the English and French guys got in a huddle to pray together after the play-off; that’s a fabulous example of how to behave.’

The island’s most ardent football fans watched the games at the Rose pub, where they serve John Smith’s beer and fish and chips. With a population of just 3,500, the Falklands are not a sporting force, boasting an amateur national football team who enter the Island Games every two years. But their athletes have been proudly sharing penguin-embossed PIN badges this week, spreading the word of the Falklands.

Their Commonwealth Games team have expressed their disappointment at the banne

‘A lot of people under 45 had barely heard of the Falklands until last week,’ added Summers.

‘You hear Argentinians talking about “Getting the Falklands back” but they have never owned the Falklands. This was resurrected in Peronist times, when Juan Peron was president and wanted something to unite the people when he was having difficulties. At the time, they were weighing up whether to invade the Falklands or to invade southern Chile to create this national fervour about taking on somebody. They didn’t think the Brits would respond but, as we know, they were mistaken.

‘In 2013, we decided to hold a referendum on the sovereign status of the Falkland Islands. When we travelled to political meetings and explained that everyone in the Falklands wants to stay British, people asked how can you prove that? So we held an internationally observed referendum. The turnout was 92 per cent. 99.3 per cent of the people voted to retain our status as a British Overseas Territory. Three people voted for something different. Absolutely everybody in the Falklands is happy about our status as a British Overseas Territory.

‘What happened at the World Cup has had some really interesting effects. It really disturbed a lot of people. Suddenly, a hell of a lot more people are more aware of the Falklands. They’re asking, “What is this Malvinas issue?”. We already have a big cruise vessel industry. Some of them bring 3,000 people. The big cruise vessels generally start in Buenos Aires or Punta del Este and come down the Atlantic and into the Falklands.

'There are also smaller, expedition type vessels that come to the Falklands on their way to the Antarctic. Around 60,000 a year come on cruise vessels and we also have our land-based tourism. It’s fantastic for walking. People come to see the penguins, sealions and the albatrosses. It’s a wildlife haven. Our tourist board have suddenly had huge numbers of people inquiring about visiting the Falklands. It’s boosted curiosity. It’s been more successful than any marketing campaign.’

Sports.title: Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months
Sports.content:
Woking chief hits out as Jermain Defoe leaves first management job after just four months

Woking confirmed the shock departure of Jermain Defoe as manager of Thursday, and now the club's director of football has said more on the former Premier League and England striker's departure

View 2 Images Jermain Defoe left Woking after just four months (Image: PA)

Woking director of football, Jody Brown, has defended the club's transfer policy after Jermain Defoe's shock departure as manager. The National League side announced on Thursday that they had parted ways with the Premier League legend, who said in a statement that it was 'impossible to continue'.

‌



The 43-year-old was appointed at the end of March and guided Woking to a 10th-place finish in English football's fifth tier. The ex-England striker won two of his six games in charge and was expected to lead the Surrey club into the 2026-27 campaign.

‌



Defoe took charge of two pre-season friendlies this summer, as Woking faced non-league side Sholing before taking on Portsmouth, one of his former clubs.

‌



Argentina players ripped apart over World Cup chaos as FIFA set to take action READ MORE :

But Woking announced on Thursday evening that his tenure had come to an abrupt end. The club said: "Woking Football Club can confirm that the club and First Team Manager Jermain Defoe have mutually agreed to part ways with immediate effect.

Brown then replied to the supporter's post – alleging that Defoe "led all recruitment and all triallists". He claimed: "Of the vast number of triallists, I did not choose one. Not one.

"Jermain led all recruitment and all triallists. All Jermain’s contacts, all linked to him. Every single one. Empty promises? We gave everything that was asked. Everything. I’m sure it’ll all come out in due course."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury fight LIVE RESULT from Anthony Joshua warm-up fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury's blistering rant on the heavyweight division

Tyson Fury brutally did not hold back in his assessment of the current landscape of the heavyweight division.

Since Fury's return, the heavyweight division has changed immensely. Following Oleksandr Usyk's controversial stoppage win against kickboxing legend Rico Verhoeven over in Egypt back in May, the Ukrainian decided to drop his three body belts - the WBA 'super', WBC and IBF - in a move which has sent shockwaves across the sport.

Murat Gassiev is the WBA champion, while Agit Kabayel is recognised as the WBC title holder. Daniel Dubois became a two-time world champion after knocking out Fabio Wardley back in May for the WBO strap, and the IBF belt remains vacant. Following the monumental shift, it now presents Fury with a perfect chance to become a three-time champion.

But when asked where he fits into the current picture in the blue ribbon division, Fury did not mince his words. "He does not. All those men have been gifted world titles. They never actually fought anyone to get one," he said on Wednesday. "Fabio Wardley - gifted a world title. Daniel Dubois - gifted a world title. Agit Kabayel - gifted a world title. Murat Gassiev - gifted a world title. How could you compare them men to me? Who's fought legends of the game and beat them for world titles.

"They're in their own little group, and I am f****** on top of the Empire State Building. They have got f*** all I want. They do not have any money. I have already had all the belts. They have got nothing that I want. And their names... they are not even high record names. Like, who knows who these people are? I know they are only just starting out their careers, most of them are a few years younger than me, but they are starting out with a no name and they have got to build their way up, and it's going to take years to get there.

"This Gassiev guy who has just won a world title, who knows that guy outside of Russia? Nobody. Agit Kabayel. Frank Warren said 'you can't fight him!' Back in 2020. 'You can't fight Agit, he's a no name. You'd get booed out the stadium.' He was only 24-0, number one rated in the IBF at the time. All these guys, they are all doing their thing. They are all going to fight it out between themselves. Even after being retired for ten years, I can still come back and get a world title shot at any time, because I have paid the price. I have spent hours and years in this game to be able to do that. I will always be a big name."

Sports.title: Tyson Fury sends immediate message to Anthony Joshua after forcing rival to quit
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury sends immediate message to Anthony Joshua after forcing rival to quit

The 'Gypsy King' was eager to fire a warning to his long-time rival just moments after stopping Mariusz Wach over in Thailand on Friday night

View Image Tyson Fury was quick to send a message to Anthony Joshua just moments after beating Mariusz Wach (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Tyson Fury is not convinced a fight with Anthony Joshua will materialise despite upholding his end of the bargain after forcing Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool.

‌



The former world champion ended a year-long hiatus back in April when he outpointed Russian powerhouse Arslanbek Makhmudov in front of over 60,000 fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Watching ringside was long-time rival Joshua - who refused to enter the ring and face off with Fury.

‌



Both men signed to fight each other just days later, but were first tasked with getting through respective tune-up fights. Joshua takes on Kristian Prenga in Saudi Arabia on Saturday night, while Fury returned on Friday evening against Wach. And despite eating a clubbing right hand in the second, the 'Gypsy King' controlled the contest before the Polish veteran eventually quit at the end of the seventh.

‌



And Fury was eager to tear into rival Joshua just moments after getting his hand raised. “I got through my test tonight. Let’s see if he gets through his test. The biggest test of it all is how big his balls are. I think he’s a big s***house. In Tottenham in front of 70,000 people, he never had the guts to get in the ring and face me. Let’s see if he ever does. I’m not convinced," he said.

Sports.title: F1 star's dog caught weeing under Max Verstappen's number in Hungarian GP paddock
Sports.content:
F1 star's dog caught weeing under Max Verstappen's number in Hungarian GP paddock

Charles Leclerc couldn't stop laughing while his wife Alexandra was left mortified after their dog Leo was caught weeing up against the Red Bull garage in the Hungarian Grand Prix paddock

View 2 Images Charles Leclerc's dog Leo relieved himself on the wall of the Red Bull garage (Image: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Charles Leclerc was left in fits of laughter while his wife Alexandra looked utterly mortified as their beloved dog Leo chose a rather unfortunate moment to answer the call of nature during a stroll through the Hungarian Grand Prix paddock. Photographers at the Formula 1 event captured the hilarious scene as Leo Leclerc decided to relieve himself against the outside wall of the Red Bull garage.

‌



Snaps show the dog squatting to wee against the wall, directly beneath Max Verstappen's racing number three. Ferrari driver Leclerc saw the funny side, chuckling as he whipped out his own phone to photograph the moment, while his wife Alexandra, who had Leo's lead in hand, appeared utterly stunned and clasped her hand to her mouth.

‌



Unsurprisingly, it wasn't long before the images spread like wildfire across social media. "Pee one for Leo," quipped one amused fan, while many were quick to crown it the standout moment of the weekend, including one X user who wrote: "Leo really stole the spotlight in the paddock today."

‌



Even the official Red Bull account got in on the act. Responding to one post featuring a snap of the deed, the Red Bull account replied: "No Leo, that is so not right" - a nod to Toto Wolff's notorious radio message from the dramatic conclusion of the 2021 Abu Dhabi Grand Prix. They subsequently shared their own image of the scene, with a note pinned to the wall bearing the message: "Leo was here."

It followed the stewards convening in Budapest and concluding that Leclerc ought to have faced a penalty at the previous weekend's Belgian Grand Prix. He was briefly examined for making contact with Oscar Piastri early in the Spa-Francorchamps race, but they opted to take no further action against the Monegasque driver.

‌



View 2 Images Leclerc's wife Alexandra looked mortified as their dog Leo relieved itself on the Red Bull garage (Image: Robbie Hoad/Every Second Media/Shutterstock)

Leclerc, who completed the race in second place, appeared uncomfortable afterwards as he viewed a replay of the incident in the cool down room while awaiting the podium ceremony, and subsequently conceded that he had escaped punishment. He said: "At the end of the day, my view in the car is that I try to push the things to the limit.

"I think with Oscar it was a bit on the other side, so that's probably not the way I want to race all the time. It's also risky for me at the end of the day. You're always trying to leave the smallest place available. That was maybe a bit too sketchy."

Article continues below

A discussion took place in Budapest before this weekend's racing, the first of two planned for this year where drivers meet with stewards to examine the application of regulations and propose possible amendments to the standards guidelines.

During that discussion, it is understood the stewards acknowledged that Leclerc should have received a penalty for his part in that specific collision.

Sports.title: Kia Joorabchian issues vote of confidence in jockey David Egan saying he ‘needed a break’
Sports.content:
Kia Joorabchian issues vote of confidence in jockey David Egan saying he ‘needed a break’

Questions were asked about Egan’s position with Amo Racing after Rossa Ryan rode a double for the team in Ireland at the weekend

View 2 Images Kia Joorabchian: backed David Egan (Image: Tattersalls)

Kia Joorabchian has issued a vote of confidence in Amo Racing’s contracted jockey David Egan.

‌



Questions were raised about Egan’s position within the ambitious football agent’s team after he was not in the saddle when two horses ran at the Curragh last weekend. Rossa Ryan, Egan’s predecessor with Amo, rode instead and was successful on both Robson De Aguiar-trained runners, notably in the Group 2 Minstrel Stakes.

‌



Without immediate clarification from Amo, online bookmaker Betway offered odds of 4-1 about Frankie Dettori, who has been an ambassador for the team since retiring in February, riding for the owners in the UK before the end of 2027.

‌



Chelmsford racecourse saved after takeover with racing close to returning READ MORE :

While Dettori laughed off the suggestion, Egan said: “There’s been no quotes from anyone and I’d like to say no comment from me.

“I’ve got no comment on the situation. I’m declared to ride a horse on Friday for Amo, plan to ride for him on Saturday and even into next week so no comment.”

Egan and Joorabchian were together at Ascot where the Amo-owned, Charlie Fellowes-trained Treasurer finished seventh of ten in the Listed Pat Eddery Stakes.

‌



Before the race Joorabchian spoke for the first time about the situation to Sky Sports Racing.

View 2 Images David Egan: staying in Amo Racing job

He said: “Rossa Ryan still rides for me, Kevin Stott rode for me this year and David has been part of our team for two and a half years.

‌



“We treasure him very much. He’s a very, very important part of the team. Regardless of what people think of the operation and what he is, he means a lot to us.

“He’s been to America for us, he’s been all over the world for us and he will continue, hopefully, to have a very, very successful season for us. If people want to make stories about us because it suits them, that suits them.”

Asked why Ryan rode the horses in Ireland, he said: “Because that was outside the country. He had ridden all week, he had been very tired, I felt he was very tired. I felt he needed a small break and I think a break would have done him well. I wanted him to come back refreshed.

Article continues below

“Why? Because we have Goodwood, we have York, we have multiple races.”

He added: “Egan is my man, he’s always been my man. It doesn’t mean we don’t have a right to give someone a break or a rest for a day.”

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
