World.title: Australia simplifies Estonian driving license exchange process
World.content:
Estonian drivers will soon be able to exchange their driving licences for Australian permits under a simplified procedure without taking a new test, the Ministry of Climate

The new procedure will take effect at the end of this year after a decision by the Australian road and transport authority, Austroads.

The change will allow Estonian drivers to exchange their driving licence for an Australian licence without taking additional tests.

"For Estonians moving to Australia to live, study or work, this will mean less bureaucracy, while the decision is also recognition of the quality of our driver training," said Sander Salmu, deputy secretary general for mobility at the Ministry of Climate.

Estonia was previously part of Australia's experienced driver recognition scheme, which allowed drivers over the age of 25 to obtain an Australian driving licence without taking local tests.

Last year, Australia decided to abolish the experienced driver exemption and invited the countries covered by the scheme to apply for a new, broader recognised-country status.

The new status expands the recognition of Estonian driving licences and no longer ties the simplified exchange procedure to the previous minimum age requirement of 25.

As implementing the recognition requires local regulations to be amended across Australia's states and territories, Estonia's new status will take effect at the end of 2026.

World.title: Russia orders Yandex Maps to blur military and strategic sites near Estonia's border
World.content:
About a year ago, large blurry patches appeared in Russia's Yandex Maps application. In the western part of the country alone there were 120 of them.

Eesti Ekspress, together with Norway's NRK and Sweden's SVT, investigated what Russia wants to hide. Blurred, for example, are the entire area of the Pskov airfield, the Olenya airfield in Murmansk oblast, the Kirishi oil refinery in Leningrad oblast, various research institutions, and radar and air‑defense points across Russia.

"The selection of blurred areas reflects the current capabilities of Ukrainian drone attacks," notes Estonian security expert Rainer Saks.

Rainer Saks. Source: ERR

Looking at the images, Saks concludes that these are largely places that are even worth attacking with drones. Since drones are fairly small aircraft that must travel long distances, the explosive payload they can carry is quite limited.

"It stands out that these are not only military objects but also critical infrastructure," says Villiko Nurmoja, founder of the defense‑industry company SensusQ and a long‑time military intelligence professional.

"Clearly, the aim is to protect themselves from becoming targets for Ukrainians, as these objects are important to the state and are considered specific targets, and a separate question is whether some objects have been placed there deliberately for deception."

Riho Ühtegi Autor/allikas: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Estonian retired Major General Riho Ühtegi notes that hiding critical infrastructure is nothing new for Russia, since the same was done already in Soviet times, when large white patches appeared on public maps around military units and major factories.

"But even then satellites already existed, and it was known that the enemy had eyes in the sky that could not be evaded. Therefore things were hidden from their own citizens — to complicate possible espionage and sabotage," Ühtegi tells Eesti Ekspress.

Similarly, Ukrainians now have access to detailed Western satellite images as well as their own and allies' intelligence information, so they do not even need Yandex images.

Confusing choices for blurring

Norwegian NRK notes that there are many apparent contradictions among the 120 blurs.

"Multiple sources comment that it is hard to see any logic behind the way the locations are selected. For instance, some nuclear power plants are blurred, but not all of them. Also, some refineries, some naval bases, and some radar installations are blurred — but many are not."

In another place, the map blur does not cover an actual nuclear site but covers the related support facilities.

This blur is on the east coast of Lake Valdai and hides there the favorite resort of Putin and his two sons, according to reports, adds NRK. In comparison, the Google Maps app shows the same area with much clearer resolution.

In Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, next to Lithuania, there is a base station for the Russian satellite navigation system. It is completely blurred on Yandex maps but clearly visible on Google.

Pixelating online maps a relatively new phenomenon

Yandex Maps began blurring images inside Russia relatively recently: back in 2018, there was not a single blurred area, writes Sweden's SVT. "On December 24, 2024, a court in Moscow ruled that Yandex must mask the Ryazan oil refinery after it was attacked several times by Ukraine."

Intelligence officials from Denmark, Sweden, Norway, and Finland believe that the expansion of Russian bases and the reinforcement of troops along the borders with Northern Europe and the Baltic could drag NATO and the Russian Federation into a dangerous confrontation, SVT adds.

"According to sources in the Danish intelligence services, these actions may indicate preparations for a potential large‑scale conflict with European states in the Baltic Sea region. [---] The sources emphasize that Russia has not yet made any confirmed decisions regarding aggression, but preparatory processes are already underway."

World.title: Construction of 2+2 section of Tallinn-Tartu highway begins in autumn
World.content:
Work on the Käsukonna–Imavere 2+2 road section on the national Tallinn–Tartu–Võru–Luhamaa highway will begin in September and is expected to take approximately 2.5 years.

The Transport Administration and KMG OÜ have signed a contract to build the 2+2 road section between kilometres 99.1 and 107.1

Janno Sammul, director of the Transport Administration's Road Maintenance Service, said the section is an important project for the agency that will make travel on the Tallinn–Tartu highway safer.

"The Tallinn–Tartu route will gain another eight-kilometre 2+2 section. In addition, travel towards Viljandi will become smoother than it is at present," he said.

In total, the Transport Administration will have a total of 53 kilometres of 2+2 highways under development over the coming years, with a total cost of €277 million, Sammul added.

The project aims to upgrade the existing road into a four-lane highway to improve traffic safety, increase road capacity and enhance driving comfort.

The works include the construction of eight kilometres of 2+2 highway between Tallinn and Tartu, as well as collector roads, a wildlife overpass, two bridges over the Navesti River, three overpasses, small wildlife tunnels, a noise embankment and noise barriers.

The connection to Imavere will be provided via the new Paia interchange.

A safe bus stop with a waiting area, parking and a pedestrian and cycling path connecting to the existing path in Imavere village will be built at the Imavere interchange.

The Transport Administration plans to begin work in September this year, with the construction period scheduled to last 30 months.

The project will be carried out by KMG OÜ in cooperation with joint bidder Infragreen OÜ.

The total cost of the works is €42.8 million, excluding VAT.

The project is co-financed by the European Union Cohesion Fund, which will cover 95 per cent of the cost.

World.title: Ukraine hits ‘Russia’s Amazon’ warehouses outside St Petersburg
World.content:
Saint Petersburg – Ukrainian drones Friday hit warehouses for Russian e-commerce giant Wildberries for a third time in six days, this time near Saint Petersburg, triggering a fire that sent smoke pouring over the historic city.

Kyiv has accused Wildberries — Russia’s largest online retailer often known as the Russian equivalent of Amazon — of storing drone parts and helping the Russian army.

Ukraine has targeted Saint Petersburg as it steps up long-range drone strikes on Russian energy, military and logistics sites in recent weeks, calling the attacks justified retribution for Moscow’s nightly drone and missile barrage of its cities.

Russia’s defence ministry said its forces shot down some 571 drones overnight over more than a dozen regions and Crimea, the Black Sea peninsula that Russia annexed in 2014 — one of the largest one-night barrages of the war.

In Saint Petersburg, an AFP reporter saw grey smoke rising into the morning sky over high-rise residential buildings in the city, President Vladimir Putin’s hometown that is more than 800 kilometres (500 miles) from the Ukrainian border.

Wildberries said two of its logistics facilities in Saint Petersburg and one in Simferopol, in Moscow-annexed Crimea, were hit.

“Rapid evacuation was carried out at all the warehouses … according to preliminary data, there are no casualties,” Wildberries CEO Tatyana Kim said on social media.

Alexander Drozdenko, governor of the surrounding Leningrad region said three people were wounded in the attack, which saw at least 59 drones fired towards Saint Petersburg.

It was the third overnight attack by Ukraine on Wildberries’ sites in the past week.

Last weekend, eight night-shift workers were killed in attacks on Wildberries sites that saw one of the company’s main warehouses outside Moscow burn to the ground.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky alleged after the first attack that the facilities were used to “supply sanctioned components for drone production and navigation equipment.”

Hundreds of small businesses saw their inventories wiped out in the strike, triggering angry comments on social media.

Kyiv calls its strikes “long-range sanctions”, saying the attacks are justified retribution for Russia’s more than four-year offensive and nightly attacks on its cities.

The campaign has triggered nationwide fuel shortages and, Kyiv says, dented Russia’s financial war chest.

– ‘Escalation’ –

Columns of thick black smoke were still billowing into the sky from one of the factories hours after the hit, an AFP reporter saw.

Russian President Vladimir Putin spent the first years of the war trying to shield the population from the fall-out of his decision to launch the offensive on Ukraine.

But the strikes on oil refineries have triggered fuel shortages and big attacks near major cities have brought the dramatic visible consequences of the war into the homes of many Russians.

Firefighters and investigators had been deployed to the sites in Saint Petersburg as the blaze raged through the morning, Russian officials said.

Saint Petersburg’s Pulkovo airport suspended flights during the attack, resuming operations around 06:00 (0300 GMT), with around 50 departures disrupted.

Both Russia and Ukraine have escalated their long-range strikes in recent months.

Moscow’s forces have fired increasing numbers of ballistic missiles at Kyiv — killing dozens and ripping open apartment blocks.

US President Donald Trump has appeared to give his backing to Ukraine’s counter-attacks on Russia — calling the strikes “an escalation that can lead to an end”.

Washington’s attempts to mediate a peace deal between the warring sides have largely stalled with its own war on Iran raging.

The United Nations has reported a surge in civilian deaths in 2026, saying June was the deadliest month since mid-2022.

Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and tens of thousands of civilians have been killed since Russia launched its full-scale offensive in February 2022 — though there is no precise toll with neither side routinely revealing the number of their losses.

World.title: South Korean tycoon ordered to pay $644m in divorce
World.content:
Seoul – A South Korean court ordered an AI chip-manufacturing tycoon on Friday to make a trimmed-down $644 million divorce payment to his former wife.

Chey Tae-won, 65, is the chairman of the SK Group, which owns world-leading memory chipmaker SK hynix — a pillar of South Korea’s tech-led economy.

Seoul High Court in 2024 had told him to pay 1.38 trillion won ($940 million) to his ex-wife Roh Soh-yeong, daughter of a former South Korea president.

The sum — equal to more than $1 billion at the exchange rate at the time of the ruling — led local media to dub it the “divorce of the century”.

Chey appealed to the Supreme Court, which told the high court to reconsider its 2024 decision and led to the tycoon’s reduced divorce bill of 944 billion won ($644 million).

The settlement is not yet final, however, as either side may refer it back to the Supreme Court.

The acrimonious case centres on the definition and valuation of the couple’s shared assets, including Chey’s lucrative stake in the SK Group.

Seoul High Court ruled Friday that Roh was entitled to a cash payout worth one-third of the couple’s marital assets.

“The defendant’s shareholdings increased substantially during the marriage through his management activities,” the court said.

“The plaintiff contributed to that increase through homemaking, childcare and public-facing activities related to SK Group.”

Chey and Roh married in 1988, but the couple are believed to have lived apart for more than 15 years. In 2015 he admitted to fathering a child with his lover.

With SK hynix selling vital memory chips to AI computing company Nvidia, Chey’s stake is now worth roughly $5.5 billion, according to regulatory filings and public data.

Roh, 65, has three children with Chey and has built a career in the cultural space, running a digital art museum.

– Bribes –

The pair were wed in Seoul’s presidential Blue House when her father Roh Tae-woo led the country from 1988 to 1993.

They have battled over the split in the courts since 2022, after Chey filed for divorce in 2017 and mediation broke down.

The court’s original 2024 ruling ordering the payout to Roh cited a 30 billion won slush fund her ex-president father used to propel SK Group’s growth.

The court said at the time that could be counted as her contribution towards the couple’s shared assets.

But in October last year the Supreme Court quashed that argument, saying that any such cash likely stemmed from illegal bribes and therefore should not be counted.

Another question was whether the dramatic increase in SK Group’s value since the couple’s separation, on the cusp of the AI boom, should be reflected in the asset division.

“The court took into account the sharp rise in the value of the defendant’s shareholdings when determining the property division ratio,” Friday’s court statement said.

SK Group shares have more than tripled in value since December 2015, when Chey publicly disclosed his extramarital affair.

The Supreme Court had already separately ordered Chey to make an alimony payment to Roh of 2 billion won.

World.title: PepsiCo deepens Iraq partnership with manufacturing, agriculture deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – PepsiCo has inked agreements with two Iraqi partners to increase food and beverage production, boost agricultural supply chains, and create employment, adding to a string of US investments announced during Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington.

The agreements, inked during the U.S.-Iraq High-Level Business Summit organized by the US Chamber of Commerce, strengthen PepsiCo’s collaborations with Baghdad Soft Drinks Company (BSDC), its long-standing bottling partner in Iraq, and Green Iraq Company (GICO).

According to the deal with BSDC, PepsiCo will aim to increase yearly production capacity to more than 250 million beverage cases, maintaining Iraq’s position as one of the company’s major manufacturing and bottling centers in the Middle East.

The expansion is planned to create new employment in manufacturing, engineering, logistics, and distribution, as well as teach and provide technical skills to Iraqi engineers and technicians.

A separate deal with GICO seeks to increase food production capacity and agricultural productivity by bringing advanced irrigation methods and farming practices to local farmers, therefore boosting Iraq’s goal to become a regional food and beverage export center.

According to PepsiCo, the program aims to boost domestic supply chains by encouraging more local procurement and assisting Iraqi farmers in improving yields and sustainability.

The deals were part of a series of commercial understandings struck at the summit, in which US and Iraqi firms announced commitments in energy, banking, aviation, infrastructure, and manufacturing as Baghdad strives to diversify its economy away from oil and attract foreign investment.

Baghdad Soft Drinks Company has been working with PepsiCo for over four decades, and both agreements were signed on behalf of BSDC and GICO by majority stakeholder Tarek Al Hassan.

The investment demonstrates global firms’ rising interest in Iraq’s consumer products industry, as improved economic circumstances and government reforms stimulate more private sector investment and industrial growth.

World.title: Socceroos star Volpato allegedly tests positive for cocaine
World.content:
Sydney – Australian World Cup star Cristian Volpato allegedly tested positive for cocaine after he was pulled over for speeding in Sydney on Friday, police and reports said.

A New South Wales police statement said a 22-year-old man — widely identified as Italy-based Volpato by local media — was allegedly caught speeding twice overnight.

He passed a roadside breath test on the first occasion and was issued an infringement notice before being pulled over again two hours later.

This time he was drug tested and returned a positive result for cocaine, police claimed, with a second sample sent for further analysis.

“His international driver’s licence was suspended for a period of six months, withdrawing his driving privileges in NSW,” police said.

Volpato, who plays for Serie A side Sassuolo, made three appearances for the Socceroos at the World Cup after switching his international allegiance from Italy to Australia shortly before the tournament.

He was born and raised in Sydney before moving overseas and represented Italy at various youth levels.

Tony Basha, a Sydney-based coach who trained Volpato before he moved to Italy and remains a mentor, told the Sydney Morning Herald the attacking midfielder denied taking cocaine or any other illicit substance.

“He was adamant he didn’t touch it,” Basha said. “He was shocked. I’m shocked because it’s a big allegation.”

World.title: Volkswagen profit plunges as carmaker weighs mass job cuts
World.content:
Frankfurt – Volkswagen said Friday that its net profit plunged in the second quarter as the crisis-hit carmaker, weighing up to 100,000 job cuts worldwide, grapples with increasing competition in and from China.

Net profit for the three months to the end of June came in at 1.54 billion euros ($1.75 billion), the 10-brand group said, a fall of 32.9 percent on the same period last year. Last year’s figure was itself a decline of almost 37 percent on 2024.

The result was hit by a 500-million-euro charge the carmaker booked for stopping US production of its electric ID.4, Volkswagen said, as well as “negative mix effects”, meaning the automotive giant sold more lower-margin products.

The firm, which in addition to its own brand also includes the likes of Lamborghini, Audi, Skoda and Porsche, also cut its guidance for the year and said it now saw sales flat or falling up to three percent. It previously expected growth of up to three percent.

The results pile pressure on the beleaguered group, which has been suffering from slimmer margins from the sales of electric cars, US tariffs and above all intense Chinese competition.

“We must accelerate efforts to structurally lower our cost base and sustainably improve our earnings quality,” Volkswagen finance chief Arno Antlitz said. “What matters now is swift and consistent implementation.”

World.title: Iraq border in focus as Kuwait reports drone attack
World.content:
Dubai – Here are the main events related to the war in the Middle East:

– Iran blasts Trump assets threat –

Tehran said Friday that US President Donald Trump’s threat to pay for shipping damage with Iranian assets was an “incendiary precedent”.

Trump had said that Washington would start using frozen Iranian assets “that the United States has in its possession, and controls” to pay for “any and all damages done to Ships, Cargo or anything related” in the region.

– New US strikes –

The United States military said Thursday it was attacking Iran for the 13th night in a row, adding that strikes were aimed at military targets with the goal of diminishing Iranian ability to attack shipping.

Iranian state media reported that US missiles had hit the city of Ahvaz, near the border with Iraq, and explosions were heard in the port city of Bandar Abbas on the Strait of Hormuz and in Omidiyeh.

– Kuwait under attack –

Kuwaiti air defences have opened fire on incoming Iranian missiles and drones, hours after reporting a new drone attack at the border crossing with Iraq.

“Kuwaiti air defences are currently intercepting hostile missile and drone attacks following the wrongful Iranian aggression,” the general staff said in a message posted on social media.

– Trump rebuked –

The US House of Representatives passed a largely symbolic resolution calling for President Donald Trump to halt military action against Iran, delivering another congressional rebuke as the Middle East war escalates.

The measure directs Trump to remove US forces from hostilities against Iran unless Congress explicitly authorises the war.

– Houthi attacks ‘illegal’ –

Attacks on oil tankers in the Red Sea by Yemen’s Houthi militants have drawn condemnation from around Europe.

Germany said the attacks risked escalating conflicts, Britain condemned the group’s “reckless actions” and EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas said the attacks were “unacceptable” and “illegal”.

– UN chief warning –

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres said the Middle East conflict was “getting out of control”.

“It is teetering on the edge of the unimaginable,” he said.

– Oil passes $100 –

The price of the benchmark international oil contract, Brent North Sea soared more than eight percent to reach $101.93 a barrel after Yemen’s Houthi rebels struck oil tankers in the Red Sea.

The main US oil contract, West Texas Intermediate, rose 7.6 percent to $93.44 a barrel.

– Island strike –

Iranian news outlet Tasnim reported that a US missile had hit a site near the town of Suza on Qeshm Island, in the disputed Strait of Hormuz.

– Trump threatens Houthis –

Trump threatened Yemen’s Houthi rebels with “major military punishment” after they launched missile and drone strikes at oil tankers in the Red Sea.

“The US will hold Iran responsible, in that the Houthis are a Surrogate and/or Proxy of Iran, and major military punishment will be inflicted upon Iran and, of course, the Houthis themselves” should the rebels launch further attacks, Trump said on his Truth Social network.

– Britain withdraws Iran staff –

Britain said it had withdrawn remaining diplomatic staff from Iran.

“Due to the security situation, UK staff have been temporarily withdrawn from Iran. Our embassy continues to operate remotely,” the foreign ministry said on its website.

World.title: Kuwait blames Iran afters drones hit border with Iraq
World.content:
Kuwait City — Kuwait on Thursday said drones hit its side of the border with Iraq, with one Kuwaiti official telling AFP Iran was to blame.

“The Al-Abdali border crossing was attacked this afternoon by hostile drones, resulting in material damage, but thankfully no casualties,” defense ministry spokesman Col. Saud Abdulaziz Al-Atwan said in a statement.

An Iraqi security source also confirmed the incident prior to the ministry’s statement.

World.title: Iraq, Iran sign transport, rail deals after Tehran talks
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraq and Iran inked an agreement and three memorandums of understanding on transportation, rail connection, and government collaboration as Prime Minister Ali al-Falih al-Zaidi wrapped up an official visit to Tehran aimed at improving bilateral relations.

According to the Iraqi Prime Minister’s office, Al-Zaidi met with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian and conducted extensive conversations with key Iranian officials such as Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Judiciary Chief Gholam-Hossein Mohseni Eje’i.

The two sides signed an agreement on international road freight transport and shipping, as well as memorandums of understanding to extend a railway connecting Kermanshah, Khosravi, Khanqin, and Baghdad, establish a twinning agreement between Baghdad and Tehran municipalities, and collaborate on government administration and human resource training.

Iraqi ministers in charge of foreign affairs, electricity, and finance, as well as the head of the Planning Commission, signed the agreements in the presence of Al-Zaidi and Pezeshkian.

The proposed railway extension would improve overland transportation links between Iraq and Iran, as part of Baghdad’s larger plans to expand regional trade corridors and improve cross-border connectivity through investments in rail, road, and logistics infrastructure.

The visit takes place as Iraq aims to retain tight economic and political connections with neighboring Iran while simultaneously developing partnerships with the United States and Gulf nations as part of a larger drive to diversify investment and boost regional cooperation.

According to the New York Times, Iran rejected a US cease-fire proposal delivered by Al-Zaidi during the visit, while Iraqi authorities made no public comment on the claim.

World.title: Police identify 2,500 people with criminal records at Jantar Mantar protest through facial recognition cameras
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has identified more than 2,500 people with criminal backgrounds through Facial Recognition System deployed around the protest site at Jantar Mantar, news agency PTI reported, citing sources.

"The technology has so far helped identify over 2,500 persons with criminal antecedents. It acts as a strong deterrent and allows us to keep a close watch on those who may attempt to misuse the protest to create law and order problems," sources told PTI.

According to the sources, the FRS units have been positioned at key entry and exit points around the protest site and are directly linked to the Delhi Police database.

"The objective is to ensure that people with criminal backgrounds do not exploit the protest to create law and order issues," sources told PTI.

"The system is connected with the Delhi Police database and can identify wanted criminals, absconders, history-sheeters, and Bad Characters (BCs) whose details already exist in police records," they added.

According to an officer, the FRS does not target ordinary protesters but is meant to identify those with criminal antecedents who may attempt to take advantage of large gatherings."

These are high-resolution cameras capable of capturing facial images even from a distance.





Once a face is captured, it is quickly matched with the police database. If a wanted or absconding accused is detected, the concerned police unit is immediately alerted, and legal action can be initiated without delay," he said.

Police said the technology will also help identify habitual offenders who have repeatedly figured in criminal cases and are listed as "Bad Characters" in Delhi Police records."

The deployment acts as both a preventive and investigative tool. It helps us remain alert against anti-social elements who may try to infiltrate the protest, create a nuisance, or disturb law and order," another officer said.

The installation of the FRS forms part of enhanced security arrangements around Jantar Mantar.

World.title: 'Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video
World.content:
Thank you, friends': PM Modi hails 'love, support' of youth in new Insta video

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday thanked young people for watching his video on examination reforms and sharing their suggestions.In a video message shared on Instagram, PM Modi expressed appreciation for the response to his address and the feedback received from students and young people."Thank you friends. I had the opportunity to meet you late last night. I appreciate the way you responded to my video and your positive suggestions. Thanks to everyone..." PM Modi said."Last night, I got the opportunity to interact with you. The way you responded to the video I posted and shared your positive suggestionsâthanks to everybody. Your love and support continue, and that our connection grows even stronger and more active," he further said.The caption of the video read: "Thanks to the youngsters who watched my video yesterday and sent insightful suggestions."PM Modi's message comes a day after he announced that the government would introduce stricter measures to tackle examination paper leaks amid nationwide protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET-UG examination.In a video message on Thursday, PM Modi said the Union Cabinet would consider a draft Bill providing for fast-track courts and stringent punishment for those involved in paper leak cases, with efforts to pass the legislation in Parliament during the coming week."I know that paper leak is not an ordinary issue. It is very painful for lakhs of students and their guardians," the Prime Minister had said, adding that the government had already arrested those responsible and ensured that nearly 22 lakh students were able to retake the examination without losing an academic year.He had also said the proposed legislation would include provisions for fast-track courts and tougher penalties to strengthen the integrity of the country's examination system.The announcement came amid widespread protests over the alleged NEET-UG paper leak. Earlier this week, PM Modi also told the NDA Parliamentary Party that the government was working to make the country's examination system "foolproof".

World.title: Grain, not guns: MEA rejects Russia's claim on deadly ship attack that killed 4 Indians
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday said the merchant vessel MV Golden Leo, which was struck in a Russian attack off Ukraine's Odesa port earlier this week, was carrying grain and not military cargo, effectively rejecting Moscow's assertion that the ship was transporting weapons for Ukraine.

Responding to questions on the Russian claim, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the information available with the Indian government showed the Guinea-Bissau-flagged vessel had loaded grain before leaving Odesa.

"As per information made available to us from the Directorate General of Maritime Administration, India, MV Golden Leo, the Guinea-Bissau-flagged commercial vessel involved in the tragic incident in the Odesa port, had loaded grain as cargo prior to its departure on July 19," Jaiswal said at the ministry's weekly media briefing.

"We once again reiterate that commercial shipping and seafarers must not be targeted under any circumstances," he added.

The clarification came days after a Russian strike on the merchant vessel killed 10 people, including four Indian seafarers, marking the first deaths of Indian sailors since the Russia-Ukraine war began.

India reiterates concerns to Russia

Jaiswal said external affairs minister S Jaishankar reiterated India's position during his meeting with Russian foreign minister Sergey Lavrov in Manila on Wednesday.





India had also summoned Russian Charge d'Affaires Vladimir Ladanov on Tuesday to convey its "grave concerns" and "unequivocal condemnation" of the attack on the commercial vessel.

The move followed remarks by Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov, who defended Russia's actions, saying Moscow would continue targeting vessels carrying arms for Ukraine.

Peskov said Russian forces would continue striking ships involved in transporting "ammunition, weapons, and so on" for the Kyiv government.

India's latest statement, citing cargo details provided by the directorate general of maritime administration, contradicts that assertion.

Shipping attacks under scrutiny

MV Golden Leo, carrying 17 crew members including five Indians, was hit by Russian cruise missiles while leaving the Ukrainian port of Odesa.

The attack has intensified India's concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the conflict zone.

Separately, the MEA also condemned another attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping "unacceptable" and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and the uninterrupted flow of global trade.

With two fatal incidents involving Indian seafarers in less than a week, India has repeatedly stressed that civilian merchant vessels and their crews must not be targeted during the ongoing conflict.

World.title: Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending
World.content:
Fast-track special courts slow as backlog mounts; nearly 2.5 lakh cases pending

BENGALURU: At a time when Centre has announced setting up of Fast-Track Courts (FTC) to ensure expeditious trials in paper leak cases in the wake of the 2026 NEET fiasco, the countryâs Fast-Track Special Courts (FTSCs) â operating under the most recent scheme introduced in Oct 2019 â are buckling under mounting backlogs.Govt data analysed by TOI shows that annual disposals by FTSCs, created to deliver swift justice in some of the most sensitive criminal cases (rape and Pocso), dropped to 66,500 cases in 2025, down from a record 85,595 in 2024, a decline of more than 22%. At the same time, pending cases rose from a little more than 2 lakh at the end of 2024 to nearly 2.5 lakh by the close of 2025.The trend suggests that despite expanding judicial capacity, fresh cases continue to outnumber disposals. Since 2021, pendency has increased by nearly one-third, from around 1.8 lakh to nearly 2.5 lakh , even as annual disposals almost doubled between 2021 and 2024 before falling last year.The figures point to a structural challenge rather than a temporary slowdown. Fast-track courts were conceived to shorten the time victims wait for justice, but rising case inflows, judicial vacancies, infrastructure constraints and limited courtroom capacity have continued to push pendency upwards.The result is that courts designed to accelerate trials are themselves carrying growing backlogs.As per the latest information from the govt, the FTSC scheme currently operates 775 courts, including 398 exclusive POCSO courts, across the country. This is against a target of at least 790 courts that should have been functional. The courts have disposed of nearly 3.9 lakh cases since inception. Yet with nearly 2.5 lakh cases still pending, the gains have not translated into a sustained reduction in backlog.The experience varies widely across States. While some States have managed comparatively low pendency per court, others continue to operate under far heavier workloads, indicating that the effectiveness of the scheme depends not only on the number of courts but also on staffing, infrastructure and the volume of new cases entering the system.The latest figures relate specifically to Fast Track Special Courts (FTSCs), which are a separate scheme launched by the Centre in Oct 2019 to hear rape and Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act cases, which has since been extended up to Sept 30, 2026. These should not be confused with the original Fast Track Courts (FTCs), which were introduced nearly two decades earlier â 880 of which are functional currently.These courts had disposed of more than 13 lakh cases in 2025, up from 11.7 lakh in 2024, but lower than 15.2 lakh in 2023. However, year-wise pendency data on FTCs wasnât immediately available. The department of justiceâs dashboard, which was accessible as of July 23 night, was offline on Friday.History Of Fast-Track CourtsIndiaâs first FTCs were established in 2000 following the recommendations of the 11th Finance Commission. The idea was to create additional courts on a temporary basis to clear long-pending sessions cases and reduce the number of undertrial prisoners.The Centre funded the scheme until March 31, 2011, after which States were expected to use their own resources. While several States retained or expanded FTCs, others allowed them to lapse, leading to wide variations across the country.The policy then evolved after the 2012 Nirbhaya case, as public pressure mounted for quicker trials in sexual offence cases. The 14th Finance Commission later supported the creation of 1,800 Fast Track Courts using the increased fiscal space available to States, though without dedicated central funding.And, in Oct 2019 the FTSCs scheme under the Nirbhaya Fund was launched. Since then, the ordinary FTCs remain the responsibility of state govts and high courts, while the Centre funds only the FTSC scheme.

World.title: Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident
World.content:
Indian seafarer killed after ship attacked in Black Sea; MEA condemns incident

NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Friday condemned the attack on the commercial vessel MV OMORFI in the Black Sea that killed an Indian national, calling attacks on commercial shipping 'unacceptable' and urging all parties to ensure the safety of maritime navigation and global trade.The incident took place on July 18, when the MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. According to the MEA, there were 10 crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. One Indian citizen was killed in the attack, while the other two Indians are reported to be safe.In a statement, the MEA said, "On 18 July 2026, the commercial vessel MV OMORFI was attacked while transiting the Black Sea, reportedly in Russian territorial waters. At the time of the incident, there were ten crew members on board, including three Indian nationals. As per available information, one Indian national tragically lost his life in the attack. We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved family of the deceased. The other two Indian nationals on board are reported to be safe."Condemning the attack, the ministry said, "India unequivocally condemns such attacks targeting commercial shipping and placing the lives of innocent civilian crew members at risk.It is a matter of serious concern that the freedom of navigation and international commerce is facing increasing threats. India calls upon all concerned parties to uphold international obligations to ensure the safety and security of maritime navigation and uninterrupted flow of global commerce. "The latest attack comes after MV Golden Leo, a Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo vessel, was struck shortly after departing Ukraine's port of Odesa on July 19. The vessel had 17 crew members, including five Indian nationals. Four Indians were killed and one was critically injured in that attack.The MEA had then condemned the strike, saying commercial shipping and civilian crew members should not be targeted, while assuring that India's mission in Ukraine was extending all possible assistance to those affected.The back-to-back attacks have heightened concerns over the safety of commercial shipping in the Black Sea, where renewed hostilities have increased risks to civilian vessels and global maritime trade.

World.title: Three chemical parks to be set up under BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme
World.content: NEW DELHI: Union Cabinet on Friday approved the Bharat Audyogik Vikas Yojana Rasayan (BHAVYA-Rasayan) scheme for establishing three dedicated chemical parks in the country.The scheme will have a total financial outlay of Rs 3,030 crore, of which Rs 3,000 crore will be used for establishing common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities inside the parks, while the remaining Rs 30 crore has been earmarked for administrative expenditure.Announced in the Union Budget, the scheme will run for five years. While the Centre will provide a grant of up to Rs 1,000 crore for each park, the state where it is established will have to contribute at least Rs 500 crore.Govt said the BHAVYA-Rasayan scheme is expected to promote the development of the chemical industry and its value chain, including upstream, downstream and ancillary industries, while ensuring efficient utilisation of resources.By providing shared common infrastructure facilities and basic utilities tailored to the needs of the chemical industry, the scheme is expected to enhance cost competitiveness and make the Indian chemical industry globally competitive. It will also help the sector integrate better with global value chains, boosting exports and import substitution.The scheme will create an environment-friendly ecosystem with centralised facilities such as a common effluent treatment plant, treatment, storage and disposal facilities, and hazardous waste management infrastructure. Govt said the development of the chemical sector will generate employment and contribute to economic growth.

World.title: Government pushes competition in power distribution
World.content:
.

NEW DELHI: Union power ministryâs consultative committee met on Thursday to discuss a consumer-centric framework for parallel distribution licensing that would allow multiple electricity suppliers to use the same distribution network.The proposed reform aims to improve service quality, encourage competition, reduce infrastructure duplication and give consumers the freedom to choose their electricity provider.The draft National Electricity Policy-2026, which is under consultation and is likely to be placed before the cabinet soon, has also underlined the need to phase out monopoly in electricity distribution and introduce competition by allowing multiple players.According to officials, the existing legal framework permits more than one distribution licensee in the same area, but requires each of them to establish its own distribution network. This results in duplication of infrastructure, higher capital expenditure, discourages fresh investment and leads to âinefficient utilisation of resourcesâ.Mumbai is the only city where consumers have exercised supplier choice for several years, while the distribution network is developed in a coordinated manner under the supervision of the state electricity regulatory commission.Emphasising the consumer-centric nature of the reform, Union power minister Manohar Lal said consumers would have the freedom to choose their electricity supplier, similar to the choices available today in sectors such as telecom and aviation. "Increased competition is expected to encourage better consumer service, improved reliability, greater innovation and operational efficiency, while ensuring optimal utilisation of existing infrastructure and avoiding unnecessary expenditure," the minister said at the meeting.Power ministry, in a statement, said members of Parliament who are part of the consultative committee offered valuable suggestions on the proposed framework. Under the proposal, existing distribution licensees will continue to own, operate and maintain their networks."New distribution licensees will be able to use the existing network by paying regulated wheeling charges, while retaining the option to develop their own network wherever permitted by the concerned state electricity regulatory commission," govt said in the statement.

World.title: Ravneet Singh Bittu resigns from Union Council of Ministers; President Murmu accepts resignation
World.content:
Bittu, a three-time former Congress MP from Punjab, was inducted as a minister of state in the Narendra Modi-led government in June 2024

NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu on Friday accepted the resignation of Union minister of state for railways and food processing industries Ravneet Singh Bittu from the Union Council of Ministers with immediate effect, under Clause (2) of Article 75 of the Constitution of India.Bittu's resignation came after his Rajya Sabha tenure, representing Rajasthan, ended on June 21. He had been a member of the Upper House from August 2024 to June 2026.In a post on X, Bittu wrote, "I express my heartfelt gratitude to Honâble President Smt. Droupadi Murmu Ji and Honâble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi Ji for giving me the opportunity to serve the nation as Minister of State in the Government of India. It has been an honour to serve the people of India, especially my beloved Punjab. I remain committed to the ideals of service, nationalism, and the vision of a Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Honâble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi Ji. My journey of public service continues with renewed dedication."A three-time former Congress MP from Punjab, Bittu was inducted as a minister of state in the Narendra Modi-led government in June 2024 despite losing the Lok Sabha election from Ludhiana to Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring by 20,942 votes.He had joined the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in March 2024 ahead of the general elections after ending his long association with the Congress. Union Home Minister Amit Shah had projected Bittu as an important Sikh face for the BJP during the election campaign in Punjab.A grandson of former Punjab chief minister Beant Singh, who was assassinated in 1995, Bittu represented Anandpur Sahib in the Lok Sabha in 2009 before winning from Ludhiana in 2014 and 2019. During his political career in the Congress, he also served as the party's leader in the Lok Sabha and as its whip in the Lower House.Bittu's resignation comes as the BJP prepares for the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections, which the party is expected to contest on its own after ruling out an alliance with the Shiromani Akali Dal.The BJP, which won only two seats in the 2022 Punjab Assembly elections, is aiming to improve its performance in the state.

World.title: KEO PC is ready for rollout, deployments across Karnataka: Sharath Bache Gowda
World.content:
Karnataka State Electronics Development Corporation Limited (KEONICS), a State-owned enterprise that promotes electronics and IT, on Friday announced that it was all set for the State-wide rollout and deployment of its recently designed and developed “KEO PC.”

KEO is an open-source, low-cost, AI-ready, plug-and-play mass personal computing system built by KEONICs to make technology accessible and affordable to schools, students, households and small and micro enterprises across rural Karnataka.

In about a week

Sharath Bache Gowda, Chairman, KEONICS, told The Hindu, “We are all set for the State-wide rollout of KEO PCs, may be in a week’s time. Then we will straight away go for deployments and plans are ready.’’

To start with, KEONICS would be deploying KEO PCs across 1,500 Arivu Kendras (Gram Panchayat knowledge centers and village libraries). “We will pick each district in each assembly constituency and the best performing Arivu Kendras in the region. Each constituency will get at least four to five PCs.”

According to Mr. Bache Gowda, KEONICS was also looking at deploying 1000 units of KEO PCs across 200 constituencies. “In each district, we are picking up a government residential school, and each school will see five or six deployments. We are choosing suitable locations for deployments so that more number students, teachers, common citizens and small enterprises in rural villages will be able to use these systems conveniently and frequently,’’ he added.

A consignment of another 1,000 units of KEO PCs would go to government schools in the educationally backward Kalyana Karnataka region. Shikshana, an NGO, which currently works with government schools and Arivu Kendra in rural Karnataka, has been chosen as the deployment partner of KEONICS.

May cost more

Mr. Bache Gowda said the PCs produced in the first batch would be sold at the earlier committed price of ₹18,999 per unit. However, the production of next batch of KEO PCs would become costlier as getting the memory was going to be trickier and more expensive.

Memory prices for both RAM and SSDs have soared primarily because of the massive AI boom, which has forced manufacturers to prioritise hyper-expensive AI chips over everyday consumer computer parts. Global computer memory prices started noticeably soaring in mid to late 2025, accelerating drastically into an intense market surge by the fourth quarter of 2025 and the first quarter of 2026.

“Fortunately, we placed our orders for memory to build our PC in last November. But the upcoming batches of KEO PCs will costlier by at least by 20% to 30%. They may be priced at around ₹25,000 per unit,’’ he explained.

World.title: Supreme Court seeks Centre’s response on NEET reforms
World.content:
The Supreme Court on Friday (July 24, 2026) indicated that it would closely monitor the Centre’s proposed overhaul of the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (NEET). The court was hearing a batch of petitions filed by the Federation of All India Medical Association (FAIMA), the United Doctors Front (UDF), and others seeking to replace the National Testing Agency (NTA) with an independent statutory body to conduct the exam.

A Bench of Justices P.S. Narasimha and Alok Aradhe directed the Union government to file a detailed response outlining whether it plans to transition NEET-UG to a computer-based test (CBT) and what safeguards will be implemented to protect examination data.

The Bench also called out extraordinary measures, such as deploying the Indian Air Force to transport question papers of this year’s NEET examination, as temporary fixes.

“We cannot let such a situation go on like this. We have to focus on institutionalisation... Here, because of what had happened, you deployed the Air Force, but that is only an ad hoc arrangement, not a permanent one,” the Bench observed.

The hearing came a day after Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the NEET paper leak controversy for the first time, announcing the creation of fast-track courts to expedite the trial of such cases amid the ongoing protests led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).

‘Going 10 extra miles’

Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Union Government, submitted that the Centre was making every possible effort to address students’ concerns.

“The government is going 10 extra miles as children’s problems have to be addressed... I can assure you from my personal knowledge, it is being monitored, supervised, and everything is being done at the highest executive level,” Mr. Mehta said.

The Bench then addressed the reforms proposed by the seven-member High Level Committee of Experts (HLCE), constituted by the Ministry of Education in 2024 under former ISRO chairman K. Radhakrishnan to review the functioning of the NEET examination system. The committee, which submitted its report in October 2024, recommended a series of structural reforms, including shifting to a computer-based test. The court also referred to the NTA’s affidavit outlining the progress made in implementing those recommendations.

Questioning the proposed transition, Justice Narasimha expressed concern over the security of data to prevent further incidents of paper leaks. “Please reflect on that also and tell us... How is data transferred? How does data protection occur? That’s very important because when you shift to this, leaks could occur, making data unsafe. And the entire thing breaks down,” he said.

The judge directed the Centre to file an additional affidavit outlining its road map for implementing the reforms detailing the proposed cybersecurity framework, the designated agency for its implementation, and the safeguards to prevent data breaches.

“Computer assistance is another thing which the committee has spoken about... Encryption of question papers... This falls into the same category. If you digitise it, how will you secure it?” Justice Narasimha asked.

Mr. Mehta informed the court that there had been developments since the earlier proceedings and that he would apprise the court of the proposed measures on the next hearing.

“I have instructions to say that the government may go even beyond what the Committee recommended. I will present a holistic view if the court grants me time. With children, there cannot be an adversarial approach,” Mr. Mehta said.

Advocate Tanvi Dubey, appearing for the petitioners, submitted that they too had proposed reforms to strengthen the examination system, including a switch to a computer-based format.

The Bench posted the matter for further hearing on August 3

Growing concerns

Earlier, Justice Narasimha had raised serious concerns over the cancellation of the examination following the allegations of paper leak, describing the development as “very traumatic” for students and their families. The court had underscored the need for accountability in the face of lapses affecting lakhs of candidates, and directed the Union government and the NTA to place on record the measures taken to prevent recurrence of such incidents.

Following the 2024 NEET-UG paper leak, which had also seen judicial intervention by the top court, the Centre had set up a seven-member committee to review the examination process and suggest remedial measures.

To implement the recommendations, the Centre had constituted another committee in November 2024 and also enacted the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024.

World.title: Protest venue under a web of cameras and facial recognition systems
World.content:
As the crowd continues to swell at Jantar Mantar, the Delhi Police have deployed powerful cameras and at least three mobile surveillance vans around the venue. The devices continuously capture live images and run them past a police database to identify and isolate people with criminal records.

Also read: Jantar Mantar protest updates on July 24

On Thursday (July 23, 2026) night, additional CCTV cameras were installed around Jantar Mantar and the images were played on screens inside a mobile police control room.

The protesters have expressed apprehension over the use of such technology. “It is quite scary as we have not informed our parents about coming to the protest,” said Anushka, a first-year Delhi University student who was at the site for the first time on Friday (July 24). “We have been using masks to cover our faces, but it may not work against surveillance mechanisms of the Delhi Police. It is highly unethical of them to use it without our consent even if it is for surveillance of criminals,” she added.

Another participant said surveillance has been under way since the first day of the protest. “Drones, videographers, CCTVs have been capturing visuals of the protest. The police say it is to track criminals but what is the intent behind this usage? Also, how can AI cameras determine the intent of the person at the protest?” asked Anuj Sharma from Dehradun, adding that it does not scare him.

The Delhi Police have deployed its DP-Dristhi and Ikshana surveillance vans and a Mobile Command and Control Vehicle, which uses AI-assisted facial recognition technology to scan live CCTV feeds. The police say the technology is used to identify known offenders and investigate violence, while protesters say it has created fear among them about police surveillance and misuse of footage.

The Delhi Police have also been capturing video footage of the protests through videographers on the ground and AI-enabled cameras used by police officials.

The Drishti van was launched in February for surveillance of offenders and criminals in high-footfall areas. The other two vans, the Command and Control Vehicle and Ikshana, were also used by the police during the 2023 G-20 Summit. They are equipped with multiple cameras providing a 360-degree view and are operated by trained CCTV personnel. The Mobile Command and Control Vehicle is used to monitor live CCTV feeds and coordinate police operations on the ground.

Videographers on ground

Ravi (name changed), a professional photographer hired by the police, said that the videos and images are handed over to the police at the end of the day. “I was hired six months ago by the Delhi Police. I have been covering the protest site since Monday. We have been asked to cover any activity taking place at the protest site, especially if there are any violent incidents in the protest,” he said.

Another person who was handling a drone outside the entry gate said he was hired on Friday. Carrying a pink slip with ‘drone operator’ written on it, he said he was a professional photographer from Yamuna Vihar and was called to provide visuals of the protest.

As per the protesters, the video surveillance began on the very first day of the protest. A public interest litigation (PIL) petition was also filed by former Jawaharlal Nehru University Students’ Union president Aishe Ghosh on July 15 over the continuous monitoring of the protest through videography.

Some attendees also said there must be ways to counter these measures to protect their identities. “In Hong Kong, protesters have used measures such as wearing masks, using cash to make payments, and removing phone biometrics, including fingerprint and face locks. These aspects must be communicated to the people,” said Paul, a security consultant who was among those at the protest site.

The police said on Friday (July 24) that Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras have been installed at various locations to “prevent anti-social elements and criminals from entering the Jantar Mantar protest”. The communication from the police said that the FRS cameras have been used earlier as well during major events in Delhi, including Republic Day and Independence Day as well as during festivals. “It is completely false to claim that these cameras have been installed around Jantar Mantar in New Delhi district with the intention of spying on the Jantar Mantar protesters. Delhi Police and Central agencies have received inputs that cross-border terrorist organisations are also monitoring the student protests and conspiring to disrupt the national atmosphere,” the statement said.

World.title: Baseless allegations, says India on Pakistan’s claims of creating a flood-like situation by increasing flow of Chenab
World.content:
India will continue to share “high-flood data” with Pakistan on “humanitarian grounds”, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) said on Friday (July 24, 2026).

Speaking at a media briefing, MEA official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said Pakistan media reports alleging India is deliberately creating a flood situation in Pakistan’s Punjab province by increasing water flow of the Chenab river is “baseless”. Officials further said that the non-operational status of the Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) has not impacted water-related cooperation between the two sides and India has shared flood-related data at least 23 times in 2025 itself.

Will share data

“Like last year, India will share high-flood data with Pakistan on humanitarian grounds, through diplomatic channels as and when a situation arises,” said Mr. Jaiswal adding that the Pakistani allegations about India releasing water is “without factual basis”. The Chenab has remained in “high-flood state” in the past week as monsoon rains continued over Jammu and Punjab.

Mr. Jaiswal said that the allegation that “India is deliberately causing flooding is baseless and contrary to the facts”.

“As regards allegations relating to flood warnings, the river flows during this period did not reach extraordinary discharge levels requiring the issuance of special flood warnings. The observed flows were consistent with prevailing monsoon conditions over the upper catchments, as acknowledged by Pakistan’s own flood forecasting authorities,” said the MEA spokesperson.

Officials pointed out that despite the fact that the Indus Waters Treaty was placed in “abeyance” following the April 2025 terror attack in Pahalgam, India shared flood-related data at least on 23 occasions with Pakistan last year. Similar data will be shared as and when the requirement arises this year as well, said an official source.

The official spokesperson said the increase in river flows is a result of “natural hydrological response” due to heavy monsoon rainfall in the area near Jammu. “Attempts to portray weather-driven flood event as an upstream intervention are factually incorrect, technically untenable and contradicted by Pakistan’s own official flood advisories,” Mr. Jaiswal said.

World.title: High Court orders SIT probe into death of pregnant woman in Sivaganga district
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Friday directed the Director-General of Police to constitute within 48 hours a Special Investigation Team (SIT), headed by an officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police from the CB-CID or another specialised unit unconnected with Sivaganga district, to probe the death of a pregnant woman reported in the district. The woman’s family has alleged dowry-related cruelty.

Justice L. Victoria Gowri directed the Director of Medical Education and Research to constitute the neutral multidisciplinary medical board within 24 hours. The neutral board should take custody of the body and commence the re-post-mortem examination within 48 hours of its constitution. The Collector and Superintendent of Police should provide all assistance for the dignified transportation and burial of the body in accordance with the religious customs of the family, the court directed.

The court was hearing the petition filed by S. Fathima Beevi, mother of the deceased Afrin, of Tirupattur in Sivaganga district. Afrin was married to Mohammed Ashraf in 2026. According to the petitioner, gold jewellery of 19.5 sovereigns, household articles, and customary seer (dowry) articles were given to Afrin and her matrimonial family.

It is alleged that shortly after marriage, Afrin complained that her husband and his relatives demanded an additional 5.5 sovereigns of gold jewellery. The petitioner alleged that Afrin was subjected to physical assault, mental cruelty, humiliation, intimidation, and continuous harassment.

It is stated that Afrin informed her parental family that she was unable to tolerate the cruelty inflicted upon her. Though the petitioner and her family attempted to pacify the dispute and preserve the marriage, the alleged harassment continued.

According to the petitioner, Afrin was approximately four months pregnant at the time. On the night of June 16, Afrin allegedly contacted the petitioner over the telephone and cried uncontrollably. She is said to have stated that she could no longer tolerate the cruelty and requested that she be taken back to her parental home.

On June 17, around 8.40 a.m., Afrin again spoke to the petitioner. This is stated to have been the last meaningful communication between them. Around 9.50 a.m., Afrin’s husband allegedly informed the petitioner that Afrin had locked herself inside a room in the house.

The petitioner and her relatives reached the place at around 10.10 a.m. The petitioner raised doubts about the claim that the victim had died by suicide and said the room appeared to have been secured from outside. She claimed to have noticed visible injuries, including a prominent reddish mark over the posterior aspect of the left shoulder, and other suspicious marks on the body. The petitioner sought the transfer of the investigation to an independent SIT, preservation of all material and electronic evidence, constitution of a neutral medical board, and a re-post-mortem examination of the body.

(Assistance for overcoming suicidal thoughts is available on State’s health helpline 104, Tele-MANAS 14416, Sneha’s suicide prevention helpline 044-24640050 and Speak2Us mental health helpline 9375493754.)

World.title: CCB arrests rowdy-sheeter, seizes eight deadly weapons
World.content:
The Bengaluru Central Crime Branch (CCB) sleuths have arrested a rowdy-sheeter in Kodigehalli Police Station limits for allegedly creating fear among the public while carrying a long machete near Tree Boulevard on GKVK Road in north Bengaluru’s Sahakara Nagar.

The accused has been identified as Madhusudhan alias Katri, 33, allegedly found roaming within the Kodigehalli Police Station limits armed with the deadly weapon. Based on credible information, the CCB’s Organised Crime Squad (East) team conducted an operation on July 24 and arrested the accused.

During interrogation, the accused allegedly revealed that he had stored additional deadly weapons at his residence, which prompted the police to register a case against him under the Arms Act.

Further investigation revealed that the accused is an associate of a rowdy-sheeter from Kadubeesanahalli in east Bengaluru and is involved in eight criminal cases, including a murder case.

The Kodigehalli police and the CCB team later conducted a joint search at the residence of the accused and seized eight deadly weapons that had been illegally stored there.

World.title: Violence erupts as police, protesters clash at CJP-Left students’ rally in Kolkata
World.content:
Violent clashes broke out in Kolkata’s Esplanade area on Friday (July 24, 2026), leaving several people injured as police used tear gas and baton-charged protesters during a march demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.

Held in solidarity with the protests in Delhi, thousands of supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party and various Left-affiliated student organisations took to the streets, demanding Mr. Pradhan’s resignation, justice for students injured during the police action at Jantar Mantar earlier this week, and the immediate dissolution of the National Testing Agency (NTA).

The march began at Sealdah railway station and drew students and people from different sections of society.

Thousands walk to protest

“The education system is unfair, we are only asking for a fair system which is accessible for every student, and we have a better future,” Udita Goswami, a 23-year-old student of Zoology and protestor at the rally told The Hindu as she raised slogans.

Protesters raised slogans such as “Inquilab Zindabad”, “Dharmendra Pradhan must resign”, and “Modi jab jab darta hai, police ko aage karta hai” (Whenever Modi is scared, he puts the police forward) as the procession moved from Sealdah to Esplanade.

Apart from the students, several elderly also extended their support to the young ones. A 47-year-old engineer, Garima Kundu, arrived at the protest with a poster reading: ‘Dharmendra Pradha RIP (Resignation is pending). Ms. Kundu, who has a 12-year-old daughter, said that she came to join this movement for her child.

“She is a school-going girl. One day, she will grow up and would want to build a good career for herself. What would she get out of this education system? With these people like Mr. Pradhan in the chair, my daughter will never be able to establish herself. I don’t want that,” she said.

Several protesters also expressed solidarity with students injured during the police action in Delhi. Many carried portraits of Bhagat Singh, B.R. Ambedkar and Mahatma Gandhi, copies of the Constitution’s Preamble, Ambedkar’s writings and George Orwell’s 1984, along with hand-painted placards.

National flags and songs such as We Shall Overcome and Give Me Some Sunshine accompanied the march.

“How can any government be so brutal on its people? What happened in Jantar Mantar is barbaric and unacceptable and has never been seen before in Independent India. I have come here to support the young people and speak against the government’s atrocities,” a 66-year-old Prabir Saha, who has a small business in Kolkata.

Chaos erupts

The protest turned violent after demonstrators reached Esplanade and began a sit-in at Dorina Crossing. Police attempted to disperse the crowd, using batons and firing tear gas shells, according to officials.

Some protesters responded by throwing shoes and bottles at the police. Several protesters, police personnel and journalists were injured in the clashes. Rapid Action Force (RAF) and paramilitary personnel were later deployed to restore order.

The protesters later announced an indefinite sit-in protest at the Rani Rashmani Road until Mr. Pradhan resigns

Additional Police Commissioner of Kolkata, Kunal Aggarwal, said that a few people were reportedly injured, though the exact number was yet to be ascertained. He said that the situation is under control now and that the police were in talks with the protesters to clear the area and reduce any inconvenience for the commuters.

Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari described the protesters as “anti-national” and said such activities would not be tolerated in West Bengal.

“In just 10 weeks, we will drive these anti nationals out of Bengal. If you want to stay here, such activities will not be accepted. I heard that the students from the hostel of Jadavpur University were forced to join this rally. We will not allow this,” he told reporters.

Several BJP leaders also painted the protest as an act of ‘hooliganism’ and an attempt to heckle the journalists. The party’s spokesperson condemned an attack on two journalists during the protest. “This is not a protest, it is hooliganism by people who has nothing to do with education,” he said.

Former Chief Minister, Mamata Banerjee, extended her support to the ongoing nationwide protest condemning the brutal police crackdown on the protesters at Jantar Mantar in Delhi. She praised young students for their indomitable spirit, unwavering courage, and refusal to bow before lathis, intimidation or the abuse of state power.

She questioned the government’s attempt to shield the Education Minister instead of answering the questions raised by students across the country.

“So fearful is the Union Government of a peaceful democratic movement that it reportedly suspended internet services in and around Jantar Mantar and invoked the draconian National Security Act (NSA) to carry out preventive detentions of students - The very future of our nation. .. If those accused of destroying the future of lakhs of students continue to escape accountability, who is the government really protecting?” she said.

World.title: Farmers complain about discharge of sewage into irrigation tanks
World.content:
Farmers complained about the discharge of sewage into irrigation tanks in Madurai district. They urged the authorities concerned to take appropriate action and prevent the discharge of sewage into the tanks, at the farmers’ grievance redress meeting held at the Madurai Collectorate, on Friday.

Madurai Collector Nishant Krishna presided over the meeting. Farmers complained about discharge of sewage in irrigation tanks in Avaniapuram, Achampathu and Sakkimangalam areas.

They urged the authorities to take steps to prevent the discharge of sewage as they were unable to carry out agricultural activities. A section of the farmers also complained about waste being dumped near Pothampatti irrigation tank in Usilampatti.

Farmers said the Periyar extension canals in the Kottampatti and nearby areas need to be desilted and necessary funds should be allocated for the work.

A section of farmers complained that a check dam was being constructed in an improper manner near the Kottampatti area. The height had to be reduced so that water reaches the tail-end areas, they said. The Collector said a meeting would be conducted in this regard.

Farmers from Kallanai who had earlier complained about the indiscriminate stone quarrying taking place in the region, thanked the government for closing the quarries. They said the cremation ground near the stone quarry should be surveyed and handed over to the authorities concerned.

World.title: In new late-night video, Modi thanks students for ‘constructive’ responses
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi released a new video message around 11 pm on Friday, thanking students for their response to his remarks on examination paper leaks a day earlier. “Last night, I got the chance to connect with you. Thank you for the way you responded to my earlier video, with constructive suggestions,” Modi said, addressing students directly. “This bond of affection will continue. Our connection will only grow stronger from here. Thank you, thank you, friends,” he added.

The video came a day after Modi announced fast-track courts and a tougher new law to punish those behind exam paper leaks. In a video message on Thursday night, he said the government had received a draft Bill that would be taken up by the Cabinet on Friday, with provisions for fast-track courts and stricter penalties. He said the government aimed to pass the Bill in Parliament as early as the second week of the ongoing session.

World.title: Abhinandh PB’s dream run continues as Goa enter UTT final
World.content:
Manika Batra said it after losing to Syndrela Das in the league phase. It was G Sathiyan’s turn to say it for Abhinandh PB in the semi-finals. Two long-time flagbearers of Indian table tennis, doffing their hats in appreciation to the next in line after being vanquished by them.

“Extremely happy with the guy, especially being from my hometown. The way he has displayed courage to beat top players in the world, it’s a phenomenal improvement in the last few years. I think he has a great future, and hope to see him in the Indian senior team very soon,” was Sathiyan’s glowing review of Abhinandh.

The 18-year-old had just trumped his Chennai senior 11-9 and earned the winning point that took Dempo Goa Challengers into the final of Ultimate Table Tennis’ (UTT) season 7. Dabang Delhi TTC’s seventh straight semis entry, thus ended in defeat.

Abhinandh has had a sparkling start to his UTT journey. Despite playing only three matches for U Mumba in his debut season last year, he made his mark with impressive displays that helped the Mumbai-based outfit lift the trophy. He has now been promoted to a singles mainstay in Goa colours, and with four wins out of six and a finishing touch on Friday, is powering the home team’s splendid unbeaten campaign.

The teenager faced some anxious moments in the game, as Sathiyan ate up his 9-5 lead in no time to exert pressure. Abhinandh kept his calm and relied on pendulum services to seal the deal, before erupting into wild celebrations with his teammates.



Looking back at those tense moments, Abhinandh said: “I had some thoughts running in my head. I tried two shots which were unnecessary. But I did not go into a negative mindset even at 9-9, which helped me.”

He also expressed his gratitude to Sathiyan for the generous praise showered. “I respect him so much, not just in the game but personally as well. His words are very impactful to me, and being mentioned by him is an honour to me.”

How it panned out

Earlier, Alvaro Robles handed Goa the ideal start, shutting out Youssef Abdelaziz’s challenge in the opening rubber. The Spanish player kept pushing his fellow southpaw into the backhand corner and as Youssef scrambled to make his returns, his forehand side of the table kept getting exposed. After claiming the first two games with utmost ease, Robles saved three game points in the third and then snatched the golden point. Goa were three points to the good, with five more to come.



But the tie was about to get more interesting. Robles’ compatriot Maria Xiao went all out in attack to upset Goa skipper Bernadette Szocs in match 2. The win, only Maria’s second in 12 meetings with the world No. 24 Romanian, came after Szocs took the first game via a golden point. Maria retaliated with a delightful array of forehand and backhand top-spin drives to bamboozle Szocs and pull two points back for Delhi with a 10-11, 11-6, 11-4 scoreline.

It was all Goa from hereon. Robles combined with Indian TT’s rising 16-year-old sensation Syndrela to blank Sathiyan and Maria 3-0 (11-9, 11-8, 11-3) in the mixed doubles rubber, and the hosts were now just a game away from the final.



Abhinandh then stepped up, and made sure the raucous Panaji crowd has plenty to cheer for, come the title clash on Sunday.

World.title: No IOC scrutiny for Infantino over Trump’s intervention at FIFA World Cup
World.content:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino won’t be investigated by the International Olympic Committee (IOC) for US President Donald Trump’s role in overturning the suspension of an American player after he had received a red card in the previous match, the Olympic body has said. The IOC said that decisions made during the World Cup was beyond its jurisdiction and it hence cannot investigate Infantino’s alleged lack of political neutrality.



The statement comes after a complaint was made by a London-based NGO formally complained to the IOC ethics commission about Infantino. United States forward Folarin Balogun had been handed a red card in their round of 32 match against Bosnia and Herzegovina. However, the mandatory one-game ban was then overturned by FIFA. In the minutes after FIFA announced the decision, reports emerged of Trump having influenced the decision. Trump later admitted to having a conversation with Infantino over telephone to allow Balogun to play in USA’s round of 16 fixture against Belgium, which they lost 4-1.

World.title: Europe battles wildfires as heatwave forces 30,000 to evacuate across France, Spain
World.content:
Nearly 30,000 people have been evacuated from parts of France and Spain as devastating wildfires, because of the heatwave sweeping southern Europe, continue to spread quickly, according to The Guardian. Researchers have warned that soaring temperatures, dry conditions and strong winds are creating dangerous conditions, leading to wildfires. Emergency services are now struggling to contain multiple blazes.

The crisis comes as a severe marine heatwave grips the Mediterranean Sea. Climate researchers warned that “Dantesque” wildfire scenarios cannot be ruled out if extreme weather persists. A marine heatwave is declared when sea surface temperatures reach abnormally high levels.

France has requested assistance from the European Union’s Civil Protection Mechanism to tackle a major wildfire near its Atlantic coast, where the blaze has forced the evacuation of more than 18,800 people, including thousands of tourists staying at campsites and holiday homes.

World.title: Sameera Reddy recalls being told to wear bum pads: Experts on lasting impact of body shaming
World.content:
Sameera Reddy recently opened up about facing body shaming during her initial days in the film industry. “I was wearing padded bras and bum pads. Bum pads are wild. Someone said, ‘Your bum is flat’. Because at that time, it was just like a problem…so make the girl feel bad. In this case, I remember it was the assistant director who was a female. I was told to do something about it. All my outfits had built-in bras and pads. I was told on my face that how much built-in we could keep doing…do something about it…” she told Hauterrfly in an interview.

DISCLAIMER: This article is based on information from the public domain and/or the experts we spoke to.

Reflecting on appearance-based workplace pressures, Delnna Rrajesh, psychotherapist and relationship breakthrough coach, said that while many may dismiss these as the harsh realities of glamour, such comments reveal a much deeper psychological issue that extends far beyond films.
